title: Handling Infringement Emails in Salted
details:
LOB: All ● Region: Global ● Channel: Email ● Requester: Adithya Venkateswaran

Update

Infringement complaints come to us by email, and you reply to them using the same email tools introduced in our recent Email Conversations in Salted update. This flash shows you how to handle infringement emails correctly — starting with a quick refresher of those email workflows, so you can tie the two together.

Refresher: Emails in Salted

Salted CX supports two email workflows, plus escalation re-opens. Here is the quick recap:

Email Type

When It Happens

Inbound Email

A customer sends an email to Groupon support. The email arrives as a new conversation in Salted.

Outbound Email

A customer is contacted via chat, but the agent needs to send a follow-up email (e.g., escalation update or additional info).

Escalations Re-opens

After customer request is escalated to MO, the customer follow-ups will be received in Salted as an email case.

A few things to remember when replying:

Set the note type selector to Email before you send — that is what delivers your message to the customer instead of leaving an internal note.

Inbound emails arrive as a new conversation with no order linked, so some buttons (Cyclops, escalation to MO, Merchant) may be limited.

Outbound: from a chat, open the compose dropdown (it shows “Web Chat” by default) and switch it to Email; always fill in the “Re:” subject line.

No existing conversation? Click NEW → Email and enter the customer’s email address to start one.

Escalation re-opens return to Salted as inbound emails — handle them the same way.

💡 TIP: Need the full walkthrough? Revisit the original Email Conversations in Salted update — the video version and the GLD News Flash Hub are linked at the bottom of this flash.

Handling Infringement Emails

Infringement complaints reach us as inbound emails sent to customersupport_internal@groupon.com. Handle them like any other inbound email — but be careful where your reply goes, because a normal “Reply” will not reach the customer.

⚠ IMPORTANT: Do not reply directly to the incoming email. If you simply hit Reply on the email you receive, your response goes back to the general customer support inbox, not to the customer!

To reach the customer, use one of these two options:

(Recommended) Reply within an existing conversation for the same order and customer that is already in the queue. The order and customer details are already linked to that conversation, so no additional setup is required.

If there is no existing conversation, create a new outbound conversation and close the inbound email. Enter the customer’s email (see Creating a new conversation in the refresher above). Known limitation: on a new outbound conversation you cannot attach the order for now. This is a temporary gap — the flow still works, so proceed as normal.

Support

Please reach out to your Team Lead if you face any challenges.

Note: All of these news flashes are also available in the GLD News Flash Hub

We’d love to hear from you! As you review each flash/update shared, please record any questions or concerns in the Parking Lot Tracker. This will help us track unresolved or pending queries for future discussion and follow-up.

Global Learning & Development

GROUPON, INC. PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - DO NOT DISTRIBUTE

Action Required

• Respond to infringement complaints directly in Salted CX.
• Do not reply directly to the incoming email.
• Do not escalate infringement complaints to CTSR.
• Handle infringement emails as part of the frontline CS team's workflow.

Attachment

📎 Attachment — click to view: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1C65Nxh3R2Kbb79GdWkMecCy4jismhnhT/view?usp=drivesdk

title: Process Update — Active Memos & When to Escalate
details:
LOB: All ● Region: Global ● Channel: All ● Requester: Rajanandini Singhdeo

Update

If a memo is active on an account, it exists to be read fully and applied — not scanned for one keyword that lets you default to escalation. "I wasn't sure what one part meant" is not a reason to send it to MO. It's a reason to ask before you act.

Do this
• Read the entire memo before deciding next steps
• Apply the instruction it gives, even if one field (like ROR status) looks off
• Ask your TL first if any part is unclear

Avoid this
• Escalating because one word or field didn't match what you expected
• Treating "no escalation to Account Manager" language as if it doesn't apply to CS
• Defaulting to MO when the memo already resolves the case

In doubt? Here's the path
• Read the memo fully first — check the whole memo, not just the status field. The instruction is usually already there.
• Still unsure? Ask your TL — your TL is your first point of contact for any memo question, before the case goes anywhere near MO.
• TL not available? Flag Nandini directly — bring the memo to Nandini for a quick review, and she'll help you resolve it without an unnecessary escalation.

FYI — a related change on the MO side

When MO investigates a merchant and confirms there's no actual issue, the internal CS memo will now stay active for 7 extra days after that confirmation (instead of closing out right away). That's your signal that MO has already checked it and confirmed the merchant is fine — so if a similar case comes in during that window, there's no need to escalate it again. Just apply what the memo already tells you.

This change will reduce escalations and increase resolution.

Questions or unclear on any part of this? Reach out to your TL, or flag me directly.

Action Required

• Read the entire memo before deciding next steps
• Apply memo instructions even if some fields look off
• Ask your TL first if any part of a memo is unclear
keywords: memos, escalation, team lead, mo, resolution, workflow, customer service

title: Week 1 - Purchasing a Gift on Groupon
details:
Season of Gifting – Process Reiteration
With the busy gifting season ahead, we want to ensure our agents feel confident and prepared to handle all customer queries around purchasing and sending gifts on Groupon.
Each week, we’ll focus on a different aspect of the gifting process, helping us refresh our knowledge, avoid common pitfalls, and deliver the best support experience to our customers.
👉 Don’t forget to test your knowledge in Kahoot!
 You’ll find the link below to take the quick quiz and check your understanding.
🎯 Key Process – How Customers Can Gift a Deal
Select the deal → proceed to checkout, or they can also use the “Buy as a gift” option in the deal page.


Choose “Buy as a Gift” at checkout OR after purchase in My Groupons.



In My Groupons, click “Give as a Gift.”


Enter recipient details → add a message → send the voucher.


✅ Note: Even if “Buy as a Gift” was not selected at checkout, the “Give as a Gift” option is still available post-purchase.


🚫 When “Give as a Gift” Is Not Visible
Deal is not giftable (e.g., Goods, Extranet Travel deals).


Deal already claimed and added to the recipient’s account.


Deal already redeemed.


Deal already refunded.


The deal has expired.


Technical bug → If none of the above apply, raise a bug via the Asana link.
✅ Note: The easiest way to identify if a deal is giftable is by checking for the ‘Buy as a Gift’ (NAm) or ‘Give as a Gift’ (INTL) button on the deal page. Additionally, all giftable deals will display a gifting banner on the page (see the screenshot below for reference).



🧳 Travel Deals
Some Getaway Extranet Deals (Market rate, Booking, Tour Operator):


“Buy as a Gift” is not available, which means that customers cannot generate a personalized gift voucher.


Customers can enter recipient details in Traveler’s Information during checkout.


If issues arise (like cancellations), the buyer must contact Groupon, not the recipient.
If a customer wants to gift a travel deal that isn’t giftable, they can purchase a themed Travel Gift Card instead and share it with the recipient.


📦 Goods Marketplace Deals
“Buy as a Gift” button is not available.


Personalized gift vouchers cannot be generated for Goods deals.


🎁 Gift Cards
Groupon’s themed gift cards—like Health & Beauty, Experiences, Travel, and Home & Garden—offer curated options that let recipients choose the perfect treat for their interests. 



Once redeemed, Groupon Gift Cards are fully converted to Groupon Bucks.
Groupon Bucks cannot be used to purchase Groupon Gift Cards.
To redeem a gift card, customers simply need to visit groupon.com/giftcards and enter their code.
💡 Agent Tips
Always check the deal fine print for gifting restrictions.


Suggest themed Groupon Gift Cards for merchants where deals aren’t directly giftable.


For Travel: guide customers to add recipient details in Traveler’s Info.


Escalate technical issues via the Asana bug report link.

title: Update: Exception Handling — Final Sale Vouchers (Already Viewed/Used)
details:
LOB: All ● Region: Global ● Channel: All ● Requester: Rajanandini Singhdeo

Update

A quick but important update on how we handle refund requests for Final Sale vouchers that have already been viewed/used.

Exceptions are not available for Final Sale deals right now. This restriction applies only to Final Sale. Standard deals (deals without the Final Sale tag) are not affected — exceptions still apply there as usual.

What this means for you

Keep following the normal process — probe first, investigate, offer alternatives.
Do not deny the customer straight away. Walk them through the alternatives first (voucher gifting, checking other merchant locations, confirming listing accuracy, Goodwill Bucks where applicable, etc.) — the same steps you'd normally check before closing a Final Sale case.
If all alternatives are genuinely exhausted and the customer still isn't satisfied, explain clearly that Final Sale means a refund isn't available.

In short

• Standard deals (no Final Sale tag) → exceptions still apply, process unchanged
• Final Sale deals → no exceptions for now, but full alternative-resolution process still applies before closing

This isn't about denying customers quickly — it's about making sure we've explored every option (gifting, alternate locations, Bucks, etc.) before landing on "refund not available," same as always. The only change is that Final Sale cases can no longer go up as an exception request.

For Standard deals, if you get a case that feels genuinely exceptional (medical, bereavement, Groupon-side error), reach out to your TL — those continue to be handled case-by-case. General "I changed my mind" or "already viewed" requests should follow the standard non-exception path.

Action Required

• For Final Sale deals, exceptions are no longer available.
• Continue to probe, investigate, and offer alternatives (gifting, alternate locations, Goodwill Bucks) before denying a refund.
• If alternatives are exhausted, clearly explain that Final Sale means a refund is not available.
• For Standard deals, exceptions still apply for genuinely exceptional cases (medical, bereavement, Groupon-side error) — reach out to your TL.
keywords: final sale, exceptions, refunds, vouchers, alternatives, standard deals, agent workflow
id: Update: Exception Handling — Final Sale Vouchers (Already Viewed/Used)

Refund counts broken down by reason:
• Refusing Vouchers
• Code Not Working
• Closed Down
• Not Answering
• No Availability

Data refreshes daily at 4:30 AM UTC.

HOW TO USE IT — THE SIMPLE LOGIC

Before you do anything else, ask yourself two questions:

① Is the merchant active? → Check Last Redemptions
② Is this a pattern or a one-off? → Check Refund Breakdown

Spike = 5 or more refunds in 30 days for the same reason.

That's it. Those two answers will tell you exactly what to do next.

WHAT THE DATA TELLS YOU — AND WHAT TO DO

📌 MERCHANT NOT HONORING
Check: Redemptions last 30 days + "Refusing Vouchers" count
→ Active redemptions + no spike: Merchant is operating fine. Likely an isolated incident — handle locally. Share merchant contact details, offer alternatives. No MO escalation needed.
→ Active redemptions + spike in "Refusing Vouchers": Pattern confirmed. Offer Bucks, escalate to Super Agent / MO with spike details.

📌 MERCHANT NOT CONTACTABLE
Check: Redemptions + "Not Answering" count
→ Active redemptions + low "Not Answering": Merchant is trading. Customer may have had bad timing — guide them to retry with contact details from the deal page.
→ Zero redemptions + spike in "Not Answering": Merchant likely non-operational. Cross-verify on merchant website or Google, then escalate to MO to investigate and add memo.

📌 MERCHANT CLOSED
Check: Last Redemption Date + "Closed Down" count
→ Zero redemptions in 30+ days + "No redemption in last 60 days" + spike in "Closed Down": Strong closure signal. Verify externally → confirmed closure overrides all no-refund policies including Final Sale. Escalate to MO.
→ Recent redemptions + low "Closed Down" count: Merchant is active. Do not process refund — handle as isolated issue.

📌 BOOKING & AVAILABILITY ISSUE
Check: "No Availability" count
→ Spike in "No Availability": Widespread availability problem — validate on merchant site, escalate to MO.
→ No spike: Isolated. Check other dates or locations, offer gifting or transfer options.

📌 ONLINE REDEMPTION / CODE NOT WORKING
Check: "Code Not Working" count
→ Spike: Systemic issue with the code or platform. Escalate to MO.
→ No spike: Walk the customer through redemption steps. Likely a one-off user issue.

Action Required

• Always use the Merchant Insights Panel in Salted CX for merchant-related contacts.
• Stop using external sites like Google, Yelp, social media, or Merchant Investigator for merchant issues.
• For every merchant contact, open the Merchant Insights tab and check Last Redemptions and Refund Breakdown.
• Follow the provided logic in the panel to determine the next steps, including when to escalate to Super Agent / MO.

title: Resolution-First Approach for Refund Requests After BOT-Issued Groupon Bucks
details:
LOB: All ● Region: Global ● Channel: All ● Requester: Rajanandini Singhdeo

Update

Purpose

To improve the customer experience while ensuring consistent application of our refund policy, please follow the guidance below when handling customers who contact us after the BOT has already issued a refund in Groupon Bucks and request a refund to their Original Form of Payment (OFP).

What should agents do?

When a customer requests an OFP refund after receiving Groupon Bucks from the BOT:
• Review the customer's concern thoroughly before making a decision.
• Investigate whether there is a genuine merchant issue that prevented the customer from using the voucher.
• Consider the customer's history and segmentation, where applicable, before determining whether an exception is appropriate.
• Do not treat an OFP refund as the default resolution. Instead, follow a Resolution-First approach.

Resolution-First Approach

Before processing an OFP refund, explore available alternatives that may resolve the customer's concern, such as:
• Offering an additional 10% Groupon Credit on top of the Groupon Bucks already issued (where applicable).
• Providing an available promo code if appropriate.
• Clearly explaining the refund policy while empathizing with the customer's situation.

In many cases, these alternatives can provide a positive customer experience without requiring an OFP refund.

When can an OFP refund be considered?

An OFP refund may be appropriate as an exception, not as the standard resolution, when:
• There is a verified merchant issue that genuinely prevented the customer from redeeming or using the voucher.
• The customer's circumstances justify an exception after reviewing the case, customer history, and applicable policies.

Key Reminder

Please ensure that all available alternatives have been considered before processing an OFP refund. Our goal is to resolve the customer's concern while remaining consistent with our policies and delivering the best possible customer experience.

If you are unsure whether an exception should be made, please consult your Team Lead before proceeding.

Action Required

• Follow the guidance when handling customers who request an OFP refund after receiving BOT-issued Groupon Bucks.
• Review the customer's concern thoroughly and investigate for genuine merchant issues.
• Consider the customer's history and segmentation when determining if an exception is appropriate.
• Do not treat an OFP refund as the default resolution; instead, follow a Resolution-First approach.

title: Clarification: Final Sale Deals – Exception Refunds
details:
LOB: All ● Region: Global ● Channel: All ● Requester: Rajanandini Singhdeo

Update

Please refer to the previous update for the initial guidance.

We’d like to clarify the scope of the update to avoid any confusion when handling Final Sale deals.

Final Sale does not mean that a refund can never be issued. Refunds can still be processed when there is a valid reason covered by the applicable process, such as:
• Deal-related issues where there is an issue with the deal or its fulfilment.
• Memo-driven refunds where the memo/process specifically indicates that a refund should be issued.
• Cheating Merchant cases — this is a heads-up for an upcoming process. The guidance for these cases will be shared with agents once the process is ready and available.

The restriction is specifically for exception refunds requested solely due to personal or unavoidable circumstances that are not covered by the deal, such as:
• Family emergencies
• Change of plans
• Other personal circumstances where the customer is unable to use the deal, but there is no issue with the deal or merchant.

For these cases, please do not process an exception refund for Final Sale deals for now. Instead, review the available options and offer the customer the most appropriate alternative.
📎 Alternative Resolution Guide

Action Required

• Do not process exception refunds for Final Sale deals due to personal or unavoidable circumstances not covered by the deal.
• For such cases, review available options and offer the customer the most appropriate alternative.
• Continue to process refunds for Final Sale deals when there is a valid reason (e.g., deal-related issues, memo-driven refunds, cheating merchant cases).
• Use this clarification alongside previous updates for consistent handling of Final Sale cases.

When handling cases, please follow these guidelines to ensure proper investigation tracking and resolution:
Check for an existing Investigation in Progress Memo

Do not manually set the case status to “Investigation in Progress” without a linked memo

Confirm the issue is merchant-related


Investigation in Progress memos are for issues affecting the merchant, not for customer-specific problems.
Verify that the case involves a merchant concern before linking it to the memo.
Similar issues


If a customer’s reported problem is different in wording but related in cause to an existing Investigation in Progress memo, it should be treated as the same issue and linked to the memo.
Example:
Memo issue: Merchant is not honouring vouchers (refuses to accept them).
Customer report: Merchant is not responsive (ignoring calls or emails).
Even though the symptoms differ, they both likely stem from the same underlying problem with the merchant (e.g., the merchant is avoiding redemption requests).

We have now implemented a change in Cyclops where the option to generate a new code for an online code issue is limited to one time only. Once a code is reallocated, the option to allocate a new code again will no longer be available.


Please follow the steps below if a customer contacts us regarding a redemption code issue:


Test the redemption process for the deal to try to replicate the issue reported by the customer, using the link provided in the voucher redemption instructions.

If you are unable to test the code or if the code is not working, reassign a new code only once.

Cyclops will display the newly generated code, and it will be labeled as “(Code Reallocated)” for better visibility.

If the customer continues to face issues, follow the Zingtree path and assist based on the customer’s preference.

For INLT, since there is no option to reallocate the code, proceed with the next option available in Zingtree.


Note: 


Always test the code wherever possible before reassigning it.

If the code still does not work and requires escalation to MO, please escalate with the appropriate error screenshot (if provided by the customer).

details:

To ensure consistent handling and accurate resolution, the criteria for the Single-Day Closure process has been updated.
Previously, this path was applied broadly to any reported closure. Effective immediately, agents must follow a mandatory checklist (Deal Page, Fine Print, and T&Cs review) to determine deal flexibility before proceeding.
Agents must now clearly distinguish between:
Restricted Deals (Single-Day Closure Path):
 Deals that are strictly date-specific where the customer has no alternative usage option (e.g., 3PIP, Final Sale, or Single-Date event vouchers).
Flexible Local Deals (Standard Path):
 Deals that can be used across multiple dates. If a merchant is closed on a specific day, customers are expected to utilize the voucher on another valid date within the redemption period.
This update is introduced to improve visibility across LOBs and prevent incorrect application of the Single-Day Closure process for standard local deals.



When a customer reports that a merchant is closed for a single day (e.g., weather-related or temporary closure), follow the below steps:
Step 1: Identify the Deal Category
Verify if the deal is 3PIP, Final Sale, or Single-Date specific
If Yes → Proceed with the Single-Day Closure path
Step 2: Perform Mandatory Checklist Audit (For all other Local Deals)
Deal Page: Check if alternate usage dates are available
Fine Print: Identify any restrictions limiting usage to a specific date
T&Cs: Confirm absence of clauses such as “valid only on” or weather-based limitations
Step 3: Determine the Resolution
If the voucher can be used on another day → Do NOT use Single-Day Closure path; guide the customer to revisit on a different date
If the voucher cannot be used on another day → Proceed with the Single-Day Closure path. [Applicable only for 3PIP, Final Sale and Single dated event].

title: Final Phase of Our Salesforce → SaltedCX Migration
details:
Org: CS ● LOB: All ● Region: Global ●  Channel: All

What’s this about?
Since October last year, we have been on a mission to replace Salesforce with a simpler, more scalable, and more intuitive solution that supports our long-term transformation.

That solution is Salted.

Today:

Salted powers 100% of our chat conversations with customers.

It is the tool we use to take over when the chatbot cannot resolve an issue.

It is becoming the central platform for how we manage customer contacts, operational reporting and early customer pain-points identification..

As part of our effort to simplify tooling and make workflows more straightforward, it is not sustainable to continue operating both Salted and Salesforce in parallel. We are now entering the final stages of our transition toward handling 100% of customer contacts in Salted.

Transitioning to SaltedCX 

We are aware that there are still some constraints. Outbound emails cannot yet be sent from Salted (we expect this to be done within the next 2-3 weeks), and visibility into escalated case status is limited. However, these limitations do not impact all contact types, which means many interactions can already be fully handled in Salted.

Over the coming weeks, we will remove Salesforce access from more agents while a dedicated group continues handling emails and specific escalation. As this progresses, our dependency on Salesforce will gradually decrease.

How to handle some specific scenarios without Salesforce?

Access to Salesforce has already been removed for some agents. We learned from their feedback and are using this platform to reiterate important Salted features and processes.

Memos

A common feedback we receive is that users lack clarity on the applicability of memos because they don't contain "Start - End dates."

We want to re-emphasize that the banner only displays active and relevant memos. If a memo appears, you can be 100% certain it applies to your case, as we filter out any out-of-date information. If you have doubts or need to review past, inactive memos for any reason, please ask your team leader. They still have access to Salesforce and can view them.

Also we’d like to mention, at the moment, it is not possible to link memos to specific individual cases. This is a known limitation; we will review this process in the future to assess potential improvements.

Checking duplicates and the customer’s history

One of the common reasons mentioned for continued dependency on Salesforce is the need to check whether a customer has already raised the same issue (duplicate case) or has other open cases.

In practice, you do not need to go to Salesforce for this. It is easier and faster to review the full customer history directly in Salted. Salted contains the complete historical record of all customer interactions.

Salted and Salesforce operate as a 1:1 data copy. We sync Salesforce to Salted every 15 minutes. This means that if a customer sends a new email, it will appear in Salted within that timeframe. If you want to see all previous customer’s contacts, just click this button:

Sending attachments

Direct follow-up emails cannot currently be sent from Salted, but this functionality is being tested.

You can now send vouchers and other files directly via chat, for example, when you need to send a PDF voucher to a customer during an active conversation:

At the moment, attachment visibility is limited to live conversations, not in customer journeys which reconstructs all historic conversations. This is a known limitation and we are working on it.

Escalating and/or Parking Case

We have added new action buttons in Salted to simplify key case management steps (e.g., Summary, Fraud, IMOC, BBB, Parking, Legal).

For example, if you need to park a case, simply click the Parking Case button directly in the conversation view.

For more detailed information about each button and when to use it, please review this newsflash from last week: CS Flash - Global - 04 Feb 2026 - New Salted Buttons - (ENG).

id: Final Phase of Our Salesforce → SaltedCX Migration

title: Final Sale Flag update
details:
LOB: All ● Region: Global ● Channel: All ● Requester: Laura Koper

Update

Final Sale is now driven by one structured flag across Salesforce and Groupon IQ — not by free text in the fine print. The new setup went live Friday, the 10th of July.. This is a systems/process update for awareness — it does not change how MO, CS, or CO work day-to-day.

What’s changing?
• The Final Sale flag is set by Sales through a structured flag: in Salesforce at deal creation/approval, and in Groupon IQ for every edit after that. Both systems stay in sync.
• Fine-print wording alone no longer controls refund status. Writing “all sales final” or “no refunds” only in the fine print no longer makes a deal non-refundable — the structured flag has to be set.
• If the flag is not set, the deal shows the standard refund policy — 3-day hassle-free in NA (14 days international) — even if the fine print says otherwise.
• Setting the flag auto-surfaces the wording (“Non-refundable / All sales final”) on the deal page and at checkout, consistently across all locales and deal types this time.

Final Sale used to live in two places — the Salesforce checkbox and the fine-print text — and they regularly disagreed. That created deals that read “all sales final” to the customer but weren’t actually non-refundable in our systems (and the reverse). One source of truth removes that inconsistency. 

When Final Sale should apply

These are the agreed guidelines with examples. 

#

Category

Examples

1

Live Events, a specific date and time that cannot be resold or rescheduled by Groupon

Concert tickets, sports events, theatre shows, festivals

2

Date-Specific Experiences, capacity reserved for a fixed date/time, no changes possible

Scheduled cooking classes, guided tours on fixed dates

3

Perishable / Custom Goods, made to order, personalised or perishable (if it requires redemption, configure it as POV instead)

Custom photo products, personalised gifts, food delivery

4

Digital Goods / Downloads, immediately accessible and cannot be "returned" (if it requires redemption, configure it as POV instead)

Online courses, software licences, digital subscriptions

5

Contractual / Legal Requirement, merchant agreement or law requires non-refundable terms

Certain medical/wellness treatments, legal services


See the full update for sales here.

Action Required

• Recognize that Final Sale status is now controlled by a structured flag in Salesforce/Groupon IQ.
• Do not rely solely on fine print wording (e.g., "all sales final") to determine a deal's refund status.
• If the Final Sale flag is not set, apply the standard refund policy (3-day NA, 14-day international), even if fine print suggests otherwise.
keywords: final sale, flag, salesforce, groupon iq, refund policy, fine print, non-refundable

title: Promo Code Issuance Guidelines
details:
Org: CS, ERT ●  LOB: All ● Region: Global ●  Channel: All 

To ensure promo codes are offered appropriately and never in situations where they may be insensitive, misleading, or non-compliant. This update defines clear exclusion scenarios and the correct handling approach for agents.

Promo codes should not be offered to customers in the following situations, as doing so can create compliance, financial, or customer-experience issues:

Highly Sensitive or High-Risk Cases
❌ Legal Escalation - A customer states they are consulting a lawyer and intend to take legal action due to an injury allegedly caused during a merchant experience.

❌ Chargeback in Progress - The customer has filed a chargeback with their bank and contacts support requesting a promo code “while this is being reviewed.”

❌ Fraud or Account Abuse Investigation - An account is flagged for voucher reselling or unusual redemption patterns. The customer requests a promo code due to “account inconvenience.”

❌ Data Privacy / Security Complaint - A customer reports their personal information was exposed and requests compensation.

Repeated or Abusive Requests
❌ Pattern of Goodwill Requests - Customer history shows multiple cases where promo codes were issued for minor issues (late replies, confusion, dissatisfaction).

❌ Threatening Behavior to Obtain Compensation - Customer states: “If I don’t get a promo code, I’ll leave a bad review / contact the media / escalate publicly.”

❌ Multiple Contacts for Same Issue - The customer contacts chat, email, and social support repeatedly for the same resolved issue, requesting additional compensation each time.

❌ Negotiation Attempts Outside Policy - Customer asks for “a bigger promo code” or compares compensation with another customer.

❌ Customer dissatisfied with disclosed merchant terms - A customer places a food delivery order. The deal page clearly states a 5 km delivery radius and possible delays during peak hours. After ordering, the customer is informed that their address is outside the zone or that delivery will be delayed, and they request compensation despite these disclosed limitations.

👉 Promo codes are a goodwill tool, not a negotiation mechanism or risk-mitigation strategy. In high-risk or abusive scenarios, resolution and policy adherence take priority over incentives. Promo codes should not be used to override clearly communicated terms and conditions, particularly when no service failure has occurred

Critical life event scenario / Exceptional personal circumstance
❌ Death in the Family - A customer contacts support to cancel or refund a voucher because they experienced a death in the family and can no longer use the service.

❌ Serious Illness or Medical Emergency - A customer explains they were hospitalized or diagnosed with a serious condition and cannot attend a booked experience.

❌ Bereavement Travel / Emergency Leave - A customer had to urgently travel due to a family emergency and missed their appointment.

❌ Natural Disaster or Severe Personal Loss - A customer was affected by a flood, fire, or similar event and requests help with unused vouchers.

❌ Legal or Victim-Related Situations - A customer mentions being a victim of a crime and is unable to proceed with a purchase or experience.
 

👉 In critical life event scenario cases, the focus should be on compassionate resolution, not incentives.

📌 Bookmark this update for quick reference.
keywords: Promo code, guidelines

title: Memo-Based Refund Approvals
details:
Org: CS ●  LOB: All ● Region: Global ●  Channel: All

This update outlines the mandatory steps for processing refunds based on Memos.

The objective is to ensure agents verify:

Memo validity


Voucher redemption status


Merchant availability


Deal status

before approving any refund.

Following this process promotes:

Consistency in resolution


Policy compliance


Accurate refund handling


Reduced errors and reworkAll agents must strictly follow the verification steps below before processing any refund based on a memo:
1. Memo Validity Period
If the customer contacts within the “From” and “To” dates stated in the memo → Process the refund if eligibility is confirmed.

If the customer contacts outside the stated date range → The memo should be marked as Inactive and should not be visible.

If a memo is still visible despite the date range lapsing → Inform your TL immediately.
2. Redeemed Voucher Status
If the voucher is Not Redeemed and the memo confirms eligibility → Process the refund.

If the voucher shows as Redeemed → Do not process the refund immediately. Escalation is required to confirm that the service was not provided.
Important Consideration:
The voucher may have been redeemed before the issue referenced in the memo occurred. This must be verified before approval.
Approved RoR applies only to valid, unredeemed vouchers.
3. Merchant Closed / Not Contactable (RoR Status)
If the memo confirms merchant closure and RoR is updated and approved → Process the refund.

If the memo confirms closure but RoR is not approved or updated → Escalate for refund approval before proceeding.

For Merchant Closed / Not Contactable cases, RoR must be approved.
 If not updated, MO must review the memo and update it appropriately before any refund is processed.
4. Deal Still Live
If the deal is Inactive and the memo confirms eligibility → Process the refund.

If the deal is Still Live, but the memo confirms refund eligibility → Review the type of memo issued.
If the memo references:
Merchant closure

Merchant not contactable

Merchant operational issues
→ The refund request must be escalated for approval.
MO will review and ensure the memo is properly updated before refund processing.
⚠️ Consequences of Not Following This Update
Failure to adhere to this process may result in:
Incorrect refund approvals

Financial impact on the business

Compliance risks

QA defects

Increased escalations and rework

Customer dissatisfaction due to inconsistent handling
Strict adherence ensures we minimize errors and unnecessary escalations while maintaining process integrity.

title: Improving Bug Reporting & Correct Submission Process
details:
Org: CS ● LOB: All ● Region: Global ●  Channel: All

Update

We would like to reiterate a few important points regarding bug identification and submission standards.

Distinguishing a Bug from Expected Platform Behavior :

Before submitting a report, please ensure the issue is truly a bug and not expected platform behavior. Here are a few examples based on recent submissions:

Login Issues: If a customer enters incorrect credentials or hasn’t verified their email, this is expected behavior. However, if valid credentials consistently fail across browsers or devices, that may indicate a bug.

Promo Codes: If a promo code has expired, is limited to certain users, or is tied to specific conditions, the rejection is expected behavior. If a valid, active promo code fails despite meeting all conditions, this should be investigated as a potential bug.

Checkout Errors: Payment failures due to insufficient funds or bank rejections are not bugs. However, system errors that prevent checkout completion despite valid payment details may qualify as a platform issue.

When in doubt, validate against documented behavior or attempt to reproduce the issue before escalating.

Correct Submission Path: GBR vs. GPROD

Appropriate submission channel:

GBR: Use this for confirmed product bugs that require engineering investigation and include reproducible steps.

GPROD Incident: Use this only for high-impact, live production issues affecting multiple users or causing significant business disruption.

Writing Actionable Bug Reports: The “Perfect Bug” Framework (GO Flash - Global - 21 Nov 2025 - Global Bug Reporting - (ENG))

A high-quality bug report should always include:

Clear and specific title

Environment details (browser, device, OS, app/web version)

Step-by-step reproduction steps

Expected result

Actual result

Screenshots or screen recordings

Impact assessment (how many users/business impact)

If engineering cannot reproduce the issue based on the report, the resolution will be delayed.

Where to Correctly Report Bugs & Incidents


To report a B2C bug (an error related to a bug found on the Groupon.com website or app), please use the following form: B2C GBR Bug form

To report a B2B bug (an error related to a bug found on the Groupon Merchant Center website or app), please use the following form: B2B GBR Bug form

Mandatory Adoption of Marker.io

Full adoption of Marker.io for bug submissions. It automatically captures:

Screenshots

Console logs

Environment data

Technical metadata

This significantly reduces back-and-forth communication and saves valuable engineering hours. Whenever possible, submit bugs through Marker.io to ensure completeness and accuracy.

Note: Make sure you check out the video version of this update so you can see exactly how to use Marker.io to report bugs.

title: Inbound and Outbound Emails in Salted
details:
Org: CS & MO ● LOB: All ● Region: All ●  Channel: Email

Update

Salted CX now supports two email workflows to help agents communicate with customers via email directly from the platform:
Email Type
When It Happens
Inbound Email
A customer sends an email to Groupon support. The email arrives as a new conversation in Salted.
Outbound Email
A customer is contacted via chat, but the agent needs to send a follow-up email (e.g., escalation update or additional info).
Escalations Re-opens
After customer request is escalated to MO, the customer follow-ups will be received in Salted as an email case. 


Inbound Emails
When a customer sends an email to Groupon support, it arrives in Salted as a new conversation. The agent will see the email content displayed directly in the conversation panel.
1.1 What You Will See
When an inbound email arrives, the conversation will display the customer’s email address, subject line, and full email body:

Key elements on screen:
•       Customer email address – shown at the top of the conversation.
•       Subject line – highlighted in yellow within the email body area.
•       Email body – the full message from the customer, including signature.
•       Action buttons – the toolbar at the top (Cyclops, MO, Merchant, etc.).
⚠ IMPORTANT: Since inbound emails arrive as new conversations without order details, some action buttons will be limited. Buttons like Cyclops, escalation to MO, and Merchant may not be available because there is no order linked to the conversation.

 
1.2 How to Reply to an Inbound Email
When you join the conversation, you can reply directly to the customer’s email:

Steps to reply:
1.     Join the conversation from the queue.
2.     Review the customer’s email in the conversation thread.
3.     Make sure the note type selector is set to Email (this ensures the reply goes to the customer).
4.     Compose your email reply in the text area at the bottom.
5.     Attach any files if needed using the attachment icon.
6.     Click the Send button to send the reply.
    
💡 TIP: You can add attachments to your email replies. Use the attachment icon next to the text area to upload files before sending.

 
Outbound Emails
For conversations where the customer initially contacted us via chat, but you need to send a follow-up email (e.g., to share an escalation update or additional information), you can now switch from chat to email mode directly within the same conversation.
2.1 How to Switch to Email Mode
To send an outbound email from an active chat conversation:
1.     In the message compose area, click on the message type selector dropdown (by default it shows “Web Chat”).
2.     A dropdown menu will appear showing the available channels: Web Chat, Email, Internal Note, and External Note.
3.     Under the Email section, select the customer’s email address to switch the compose mode to email.

2.2 Composing and Sending the Email
Once you switch to email mode, the compose area changes to show email fields:

Steps to compose and send:
1.     The customer’s email address will be auto-filled in the recipient field.
2.     Fill in the subject line in the “Re: SUBJECT” field. This is a critical step – do not leave it blank!
3.     Write your email message in the body area.
4.     Attach any files if needed using the attachment icon.
5.     Click the Send button to deliver the email to the customer.
⚠ IMPORTANT: Always remember to add a subject to the email in the "Re:" section. Sending an email without a subject line may confuse the customer and looks unprofessional. Write a clear, descriptive subject that helps the customer understand the context of your message.

 
2.3 Creating a New conversation
To send an outbound email when there is no active conversations with this customer:
1.     In the top section, click on the option NEW -> Email

2.     An option will appear to add the email address you want to send an email:

3.     Under the Email section, select the customer’s email address to switch the compose mode to email.

Escalations Re-opens
When a customer request has been escalated to the Merchant Operations team to handle, the customer responses after the case has been considered resolved will be received back in Salted. 
You will need to manage as an Inbound Email and respond to customer via email.

title: Automated Memo Creation for Merchant-Related Issues (Bot → MO Direct)
details:
LOB: All ● Region: Global ● Channel: All ● Requester: Laura Koper

Update

1. What’s changing

Scope: Local deals only. Enterprise and other account types are excluded for now.

When a customer reports a merchant-wide issue to the chatbot — merchant closed, not honoring, or not contactable — the bot itself now handles the escalation end-to-end:

Checks the account for an existing active or in-progress memo

If none exists, asks the customer clarifying questions (“closed last Saturday for me” vs. “permanently closed”) to separate customer-specific complaints from merchant-wide issues

Creates an internal “Investigation in Progress” memo on the account

Escalates the case directly to the MO queue, linked to that memo

⚠ The key change for you: these cases arrive without a CS agent having touched them. No CS triage, no agent notes — the bot conversation summary in the case description is your full context. Read it first.

If an active memo already exists, new customer reports on the same issue are linked to the existing memo instead of creating duplicates — only the first case lands in the MO queue.

2. What the automated memo looks like

Status

Active · INTERNAL ONLY — the bot never creates external memos; once you confirm the issue with the partner, you create the External CS MEMO (see section 4)

Duration

7 days

Content

Short summary of the reported issue + link to the bot conversation

Created by

“Customer Support integration” — that’s how you know it’s automated

Linking

Account level (no opportunity attached) by default — these issues usually affect the whole account, and it prevents duplicate memos when other customers report the same problem on different deals. Exception: if the case is clearly about only one deal/opportunity or location, adjust the memo to that opportunity (see section 4)

Case

The triggering case appears under the memo’s Related Cases, and the first case is flagged as “MEMO Parent case”

3. What stays on the old path (for now)

Customer-specific issues (one customer’s bad experience, not a merchant-wide problem) → routed to CS agents as today, no memo created

Customers who insist on a human (“agent, agent, agent”) → go to a CS agent, who escalates to MO without an auto-memo. Extending memo creation to this path is agreed but comes later.

Expect a mix of memo-linked and memo-less merchant-issue cases in the queue initially. Both are normal.

4. What you need to do

Work the case, not the memo. Handle it like any other merchant-issue case.

Start from the bot conversation summary in the case description — it replaces the CS agent notes you’re used to. If the summary/transcript is missing, log it in the feedback tracker (known item being verified).

Check the “MEMO Parent case” flag. Only the first case on a memo should carry it — verify it’s set on the parent case (and not on subsequent linked cases).

Contact the merchant as usual — send the standard communication.

Review the memo and check its scope. If the escalation is clearly about only one deal/opportunity or location, adjust the memo to that opportunity instead of leaving it account-wide. Otherwise, leave the memo as created — don’t edit it unless something is genuinely wrong (wrong account, wrong issue type, incorrect details).

Once the issue with the partner is confirmed, create an “External CS MEMO”. The bot only ever creates the internal “Investigation in Progress” memo — making the confirmed status visible to CS is your responsibility, same as today. Don’t let the auto-created internal memo make you skip this step.

If a memo was created incorrectly, report it in the feedback tracker. We especially need examples of memos created for customer-specific issues that shouldn’t have a memo at all, and cases where you had to narrow the scope to one deal/location (so we can tune the automation).

Investigate before attaching cases to a memo. An existing memo is not a shortcut — confirm the new case is genuinely the same merchant-wide issue before linking or resolving against it.

When there is not enough information to escalate to the merchant, the standard process of transferring the case back to CS still applies. When that happens, please report it in the feedback tracker and put the created internal CS memo by the bot on inactive

If there is not enough information to escalate any of the cases linked to a memo (for example, location details are missing across all linked cases), transfer all linked cases back to CS to gather the missing information, set the internal memo to Inactive, and report it in the feedback tracker. Do not leave the memo active if no case can move forward. 

5. Do / Don’t at a glance

✓ Do

✗ Don’t

Work the case from the MO queue as usual

Read the bot conversation summary first

Contact the merchant with standard comms

Create an External CS MEMO once the issue with the partner is confirmed

Verify the “MEMO Parent case” flag is on the first case only

Narrow the memo to a specific deal/location when the issue is clearly limited to it

Review the memo; report issues via the tracker

Verify it’s the same merchant-wide issue before attaching a case

When the issue is not enough info and you have to transfer the case back to CS, put the created internal CS memo by the bot on inactive

If no linked case has enough info to escalate, transfer all back to CS, set the memo to Inactive, and log it in the tracker. 

Change memo status, dates, or internal flag — internal, 7-day active is expected behavior (narrowing scope to one deal/location is the one expected edit)

Create a second memo for the same issue — check Related Cases first

Add the case number to the memo manually — it’s visible via Related Cases

Flag subsequent linked cases as “MEMO Parent case” — first case only

Treat “there’s a memo” as a reason to skip investigation

6. Why this matters

Repetitive merchant-issue contacts (especially small merchants) generate many duplicate conversations today. With the bot checking for an active memo before escalating, the next customer reporting the same merchant gets deflected immediately instead of creating another case.

Because CS agents are no longer in the loop for these escalations, MO queue volumes may shift — we will monitor accuracy and escalation volume closely during the first weeks, the same way we did for the January/February changes.

Action Required

• Read the bot conversation summary in the case description first for full context.
• Verify the "MEMO Parent case" flag, contact the merchant, and review/narrow the memo's scope.
• Create the External CS MEMO once the issue is confirmed with the partner.
• Do not change memo status, dates, or internal flag; do not create duplicate memos; do not skip investigation. Report incorrect memos or missing transcripts via the feedback tracker.
keywords: memo, bot, merchant issues, escalation, mo queue, agent workflow, local deals
id: Automated Memo Creation for Merchant-Related Issues (Bot → MO Direct)

title: Empathy-first mindset to Resolution-first mindset
details:
Org: CS ● LOB: All ● Region: Global ●  Channel: All

Update


In chat and email interactions, responses tend to prioritize long apologies and emotional validation. While this reflects a desire to show care, data confirms that excessive empathy impacts productivity and slows resolution speed.


Most importantly, it delays what the customer actually wants: A Fix


The Impact of Current Habits:

Reduced Speed: Long paragraphs of apologies take time to write and time for the customer to read.

Diluted Focus: The actual solution gets buried under "fluff."

Customer Perception: Customers value a fast solution more than a long apology.

Customers value speed and clarity more than extended apologies. Do not tell the customer how sorry you are for three sentences. Show them you can fix it in one.

Going forward, our primary goal is Resolution Efficiency. We are shifting from emotional validation to operational confidence. 

The rule is simple: lead with action. Keep acknowledgment brief and transition immediately into solving so customers see progress right away. 


Action Required


1️⃣ Follow the “One-Sentence Apology” Rule

If an apology is necessary, limit it to one brief sentence at the beginning.

Immediately transition to the solution.

Avoid: Long emotional explanations and repeated apologies.

Adopt: I apologize for the trouble. Let’s get that fixed for you.

2️⃣ Lead with action
Acknowledge the issue briefly and move immediately into an action statement. The solution or action plan should be visible in the first paragraph (email) or the first few messages (chat).

Use short bridging phrases that signal work has already started, such as:

Thanks for reaching out. I’m looking into this now.

Got it. Let me check this for you.

I’ll review your case and update you shortly.

Let me pull up the details and sort this out.

I’m on it. One moment while I investigate.

Let’s fix this. I’m checking what happened.

Thanks for flagging. I’ll take care of this.

3️⃣ Use Active, Confident Language
Direct does not mean rude. Use action-driven statements that show ownership.

Avoid (Passive):  “Hopefully, this should resolve the issue.”

Adopt (Active):  “I have applied the credit to your account. It is available immediately.”

Below are side-by-side examples of what to avoid and what to adopt. Each scenario shows how long empathy-driven responses can bury the solution - and how an action-first response gets the customer to the fix faster.


Scenario

The "Over-Empathizing" Approach (STOP)

The "Action-First" Approach (START)

Voucher Expired

"I am so sorry to see that your voucher has expired. I completely understand how frustrating it is to lose out on a deal you paid for.

“The promotional window for this deal ended on [Date]. However, the amount you paid never expires. You should still be able to use the voucher with the merchant."

Invalid Code" Error

"I apologize sincerely for the technical difficulties you are facing with the redemption code. I know how annoying it is when technology doesn't work right at the register. Thank you for your patience while I look into this."

"I’ve checked the code and see you’re using an incorrect code for redemption. Please use the code: XXXXX for redemption. 

Merchant Won't Accept

"I am terribly sorry to hear the merchant refused your voucher. That is definitely not the experience we want you to have, and I can imagine how awkward that must have felt. I apologize for this inconvenience."

"Since the merchant is unable to honor the voucher, I’ve escalated your request internally. We’ll make sure to get back to you as soon as possible.

Fine Print Restriction

"I am so sorry for the confusion regarding the valid dates. I know it's disappointing to find out you can't use it on weekends after you already made plans. I apologize that the fine print wasn't clearer."

"This specific deal is valid Monday through Thursday. I can help you reschedule your booking for a weekday."

title: Champions UGC Pilot — Phase 1
details:
LOB: All ● Region: NAM ● Channel: All ● Requester: Revathi Nallathambi

Update

We're running a small pilot inviting select Champions (our most active customers) to submit short videos from a recent Groupon experience — Things to Do or Food & Restaurants only.
Phase 1 outreach emails go out to Champions on Monday, July 20.
Because Champions are the group most likely to contact Care with questions, we're briefing the floor ahead of the send.

How it works;
• Participant fills out the submission form (~2 min) and uploads a short vertical video (15–60 sec) of a Things to Do or Food & Restaurants experience they personally booked.
• Groupon's social team reviews the submission for quality and brand fit within 5 business days of submission.
• If approved, Groupon posts the content on Groupon's own social channels (not the participant's account) and credits them per their stated preference (handle, first name, or no attribution).
• $50 in Groupon Bucks is credited within 5 business days of approval — not of submission.
• Phase 1 limit: one $50 credit per participant per 30-day window. They can submit multiple pieces of content, but only one payout per window.
• After they redeem that $50 on a Groupon purchase, they become eligible to submit again for another round.

Key facts;
• The email is legitimate. It's sent from a Groupon social address, not a standard marketing send — it is not spam or phishing.
• Customers cannot reply directly to the email. They're directed to a submission form linked in the email.
• Not all content is approved. Submissions that don't meet quality/brand-fit standards are rejected, and participants are notified either way — they can submit a new piece during the same 30-day window.
• Groupon writes the caption and handles the required FTC disclosure on any post it publishes — participants don't need to do anything on their end for that.
• Resharing afterward is optional, never required.
• They'll get an email within 5 business days of submitting — either an approval/posting notice or a request to revise and resubmit.
• Submitting starts the review; payout is only triggered once content is approved.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1DXIvc4XLdyt2sQg5PphoP6X3NpvQgceT6kJFLPeq0jQ/edit?slide=id.p5#slide=id.p5

Action Required

• Confirm the Champions UGC Pilot email is legitimate and not spam.
• Advise customers to use the submission form linked in their invite, as direct replies to the email are not possible.
• Inform customers that $50 Groupon Bucks are credited within 5 business days of content approval, not submission.
• Clarify that Groupon posts approved content on its own channels, and participants receive an email notification within 5 business days of submission regarding approval or revision.

Campaign Period: May 25 – July 24, 2026

title: Clarification on Booking Tool Error vs No Availability
details:
LOB: All ● Region: Global ●  Channel: All ● Requester: Rajanandini Singhdeo

The decision tree for handling “Voucher Expiring Soon” inquiries has been updated for Local Bookability Deals, Regular Deals, and Groupon Booking Tool reservations.

Agents are expected to follow the updated decision tree and verify whether availability exists before the voucher expiration date before determining the resolution.

Please ensure you correctly distinguish between a Groupon Booking Tool Error and a No Availability scenario before proceeding.

Groupon Booking Tool Error

A Groupon Booking Tool Error applies only when there is no availability showing at all in the booking tool, including future weeks and months.

This means:

All dates are greyed out/unavailable across the entire booking calendar.

No bookable slots are visible for any upcoming dates.

This indicates a potential technical issue with the booking tool and should not be confused with limited merchant availability.

No Availability

A No Availability scenario applies when:

No slots are available before the voucher expiration date, but future availability is visible after the voucher expires, OR

The customer’s preferred date is fully booked.

If future dates are visible and available in upcoming weeks or months, this is not a Booking Tool Error. It must be treated as a No Availability scenario and resolved according to the updated decision tree.

Please ensure this distinction is applied consistently when reviewing booking-related inquiries.

title: Adidas Gift Card Process
details:
Org: CS ● LOB: All ● Region: INTL ●  Channel: All

Update

Starting 23rd February 2026, a new Adidas Gift Card deal will be available on Groupon. It’s important that you are fully clear on how it works to prevent confusion at checkout and ensure a smooth redemption experience.

How the Deal Works (What Agents Must Know)

When a customer purchases this deal, they will receive one voucher that contains two separate gift cards: a Regular Gift Card, which is valid for three years, and a Promotional Gift Card, which is valid until 26 April 2026.

Both cards must be redeemed directly on the Adidas website during checkout - not on Groupon.

During checkout, customers need to navigate to Payment → Gift Card and enter the 19-digit gift card number along with the 4-digit PIN exactly as displayed on their voucher.

It is important to guide customers not to enter these details in the promo or discount code field, as this will not apply the balance. If the total basket value exceeds the available gift card balance, the customer must add an additional payment method to complete the purchase.

Where Customers Find Their Voucher
Customers can access their voucher by logging into their Groupon account. On the web, they can visit My Groupon, select the relevant purchase, and click View Details to access the printable voucher. 

On the app, they simply go to My Purchases and open the voucher from there.

What to ask the customer 
When a customer reports that the gift card “doesn’t work,” the reason could simply be that the customers enter the gift card information in the promo field. 

Check for the following information to help the customer with redemption:  

Are they entering it under Payment → Gift Card (not promo code field)?

Are they entering only the 19-digit number (not including “GC_” or “Promo_”)?

Are they entering the correct 4-digit PIN?

Is the cart total higher than the gift card value (requires a second payment method)?

Are they trying to use the Promotional card vs Regular card (validity differences)?

Few FAQs & Recommended Responses
Q: “I can’t apply it—there’s only a promo code field.”
A: The gift card must be entered during checkout under Payment → Gift card, not in the promo code field. Please enter the 19-digit number and 4-digit PIN there.

Q: “What part is the gift card number?”
A: The gift card number is the 19-digit number after ‘GC_’ on the voucher. The PIN is the 4-digit number after ‘Pin_’.

Q: “Why do I see two codes?”
A: Each purchase includes:

One regular gift card (valid 3 years)

One promotional gift card (valid until 26 April 2026)

Q: “My total is higher than the gift card.”
A: The gift card can still be used. The customer will need to add another payment method to cover the difference.

Q: “How do I check what’s left on my card?”
A: The balance can be checked here: wbiprod.storedvalue.com/wbir/clients/adidas?lng=en 


Action Required

For any Redemption Related Queries: 

Always confirm the customer is entering the code under Payment → Gift Card, not in the promo field. Verify they are using only the 19-digit gift card number and 4-digit PIN (without “GC_” or “Promo_” prefixes), and clarify whether they are redeeming the Regular or Promotional card to ensure it is within its validity period.

Clarify that the Regular gift card remains valid for 3 years from the purchase date, while the Promotional gift card is valid until 26 April 2026.

For Cancellation Requests: Check the purchase date (within or beyond 14 days): 

If the request is within 14 Days, submit the cancellation form and reply to the customer using the Salted Snippet Adidas.refund1. If the customer asks for an update, check Adidas’ response in Column D of the response sheet. 

If the cancellation is approved, respond using Adidas.refund-approved. If it is rejected, use Adidas.refund-rejected. If there is no response yet, use Adidas.refund-pending.

Always monitor Column D of the response sheet  for confirmation from Adidas’ before processing any refund. Do not promise a cancellation or refund until Adidas confirms that the gift cards are unused. If Adidas confirms partial or full usage, cancellation and refund are not permitted.

If the request falls outside the 14-day window, respond using the Salted Snippet Adidas.outside14days and inform the customer that cancellation is not possible as per policy.
keywords: Adidas

title: CS Process Change - PayPal Dispute Status Check & Manual Refunds
details:
LOB: All ● Region: Global ● Channel: All ● Requester: Adithya Venkateswaran

Update

This update covers two process changes.

PayPal dispute status checks are no longer escalated to the CTSR team.
The agent now escalates the dispute to the SME/TL, and the SME/TL checks the dispute status directly in PayPal and actions it using the same outcomes as the Credit Card / Apple Pay path.

Manual refunds are now owned by the frontline and SME/TL.
Any refund that can be reprocessed through Adyen is handled in-house; the manual refund form is only offered when the payment method is no longer valid.
Manual refunds are no longer escalated to CTSR by default.

Both updates move ownership of these cases upstream to the frontline / SME/TL, so agents resolve more at first contact instead of handing off to CTSR.

PayPal dispute checks
Agents no longer escalate to CTSR.
They now escalate to the SME/TL (Welcome → Fraud or Legal or Data privacy issue or Dispute → Dispute status check → PayPal), and the SME/TL checks the dispute status directly in PayPal and actions it using the same outcomes as the Credit Card / Apple Pay path.

Manual refunds
Agents now own the "refund failed in Cyclops" flow — check for an on-going dispute, confirm the Cyclops refund status, and verify whether the card/bank account is still valid.
If valid → escalate to a supervisor (Supervisor Escalation type = "Manager Escalation") to reprocess through Adyen; if not valid → provide the manual refund form.
These are no longer escalated to CTSR by default.

Net effect: one fewer escalation hop and faster resolution, with a new decision-tree path to follow.
The key behaviour change to reinforce is selecting "Manager Escalation" (not "Manual Refund") so cases route to the TL/SME queue rather than CTSR.

These cases previously defaulted to CTSR, adding avoidable escalation hops and delaying resolution for the customer.
Manual refunds alone drive ~30–35 CTSR escalations per week — the majority of which the frontline / SME/TL can now handle directly.

Moving ownership upstream
• Reduces unnecessary CTSR escalations and frees CTSR capacity for cases that genuinely need specialist intervention.
• Speeds up resolution and improves the customer experience through first-contact resolution.
• Strengthens frontline ownership and confidence in handling dispute checks and failed refunds.

Action Required

• For PayPal disputes, escalate to SME/TL using the path: Welcome → Fraud or Legal or Data privacy issue or Dispute → Dispute status check → PayPal.
• For failed refunds, own the "refund failed in Cyclops" flow: check for ongoing disputes, confirm Cyclops refund status, and verify card/bank account validity.
• If a failed refund is valid, escalate to a supervisor (Supervisor Escalation type = "Manager Escalation") for reprocessing through Adyen.
• If a failed refund is not valid, provide the manual refund form.

Ask the customer to open the order.


Direct them to swipe or scroll left on the screen to view the rest of their vouchers.


Reassure them that this is normal app behavior, and all vouchers are present, just not all visible by default.
Please go through the video as well to understand the functionality for multiple vouchers in the Groupon app.


By following these steps, agents can help customers navigate the app more efficiently and resolve confusion regarding multiple vouchers.

title: Escalations to Memo in progress
details:
Org: MO,CS ● LOB: All ● Region: Global ●  Channel: All

Update/Reminder

When a customer contacts the bot about a merchant issue categorized as “Merchant moved/closed” or “Merchant not honoring”, the bot will now check for existing memos before routing the case.

If an Active memo with status “Investigation in Progress” exists for the affected merchant/deal, the bot will:

Attach the new escalated case to the existing memo

Inform the customer the case is escalated and they will receive a response by email once the issue is resolved with the merchant

Skip the CS and MO queues — the case is not routed for individual handling

Wait for the memo to be resolved by MO; the case is then resolved in bulk

Trigger the resolution communication to the customer automatically

Why this change?

Eliminates duplicate handling when MO is already investigating the merchant

Faster, consistent resolution for customers via bulk handling

Frees CS and MO capacity for cases that genuinely need individual attention

End-to-end flow
Step

What happens

1 Customer contacts the bot about a merchant issue

2 Bot identifies the contact reason as Merchant moved/closed or Merchant not honoring

3 Bot checks for an existing memo on the merchant/deal with status Active – Investigation in Progress

4 Bot informs the customer the case is escalated and a response will be sent via email

5 Bot creates a new case in Salesforce

6 Bot attaches the case to the existing Active memo

7 Case bypasses the CS and MO queues

8 When MO resolves the memo, all attached cases are resolved in bulk

9 Customer receives the resolution communication

Action Required


You will not see these cases in your regular queues - that’s expected behaviour, not a routing miss.

Cases will appear in Salesforce linked to the parent memo. If a customer follows up through another channel, check SF first - the case may already be attached to an active memo.

If no active memo exists, the normal CS/MO escalation flow applies - nothing changes there.

Standard CS escalation rules still apply if a customer is unhappy with the bot routing.

FAQ
What happens if a customer contacts us again before the memo is resolved?
Check that the case is attached to the memo. Do not create a duplicate; reassure the customer their case is in the bulk resolution queue.

What if the memo is closed but the customer’s issue is not resolved?
Standard reopen process.

Does this apply to all markets?
Yes, NAM and INTL, all languages supported by the bot.

title: Global Bug Reporting
details:
Org: GO ● LOB: All ● Region: Global ●  Channel: All


We want to be absolutely clear about the expectation going forward. All agents are now required to submit every bug through the official GBR forms or Marker.io. 

Your full attention is needed, as accurate bug reporting directly impacts how quickly issues are resolved and how smoothly our operations run. Please read the instructions below carefully. Even small mistakes in reporting can lead to significant delays for customers, merchants, and our engineering teams.

How to Correctly Report Bugs & Incidents.

To help us resolve issues faster and improve the experience for both customers and merchants, here’s a complete guide on GBR bugs, GPROD incidents, Marker.io, and how to write perfect bug reports.

This update combines all official instructions from Global Bug Reporting (GBR) and GPROD Incident Management. Please read this carefully — it helps engineering teams fix problems much faster.

To report a B2C bug (an error related to a bug found on the Groupon.com website or app), please use the following form: B2C GBR Bug form

To report a B2B bug (an error related to a bug found on the Groupon Merchant Center website or app), please use the following form: B2B GBR Bug form

🐞 1. What Is a GBR Bug?

GBR = Global Bug Reporting
Use GBR when the issue is a minor production bug or improvement suggestion that:

Affects one or a small group of users


Does not stop the website/app from functioning globally


Is not a major revenue-impacting issue


Examples of GBR bugs:
Incorrect text on a page


Wrong button color


Minor UI glitches


A page partially loads but still works


A feature fails for one customer but works for most


Where GBR Bugs Come From
Created via:

B2C GBR Bug form (for Groupon.com website + app issues)


B2B GBR Bug form (for Merchant Center + Salesforce issues)


Marker.io widget (recommended!)


🖼️ 2. Using Marker.io (Highly Recommended!)

You’ll see a red “Report Issue” button on the right side of:

Groupon.com


Merchant Center


Marker.io automatically captures:

Screenshot


URL


Browser console logs


Device/environment info


A 30-second user recording


This saves engineering HOURS. Please use Marker.io whenever possible.

How to create a Marker.io ticket:

image.png

Log in to Groupon.com or Merchant Center


Click Report Issue


Marker.io takes a screenshot


Fill in:


Issue name


Steps to reproduce


What exactly went wrong


Expected vs actual result


Choose Bug (not Suggestion/Improvement)


Choose urgency: Low / Middle


📌 3. How to Write the PERFECT Bug Report

A great bug report = fast fix. A vague report = days/weeks wasted trying to replicate.

✔️ 1. Clear & Specific Title
Bad: “Checkout broken”
Good: “[Checkout] ‘Invalid Promo Code’ error shown when code is valid”

✔️ 2. The WHO
Include:

Customer ID or email


Merchant permalink (for B2B)


Name/company


Salesforce account link


✔️ 3. The WHERE
Specify:

Website / Mobile App / Internal Tool


Browser (Chrome/Safari/Firefox)


App version (iOS/Android)


Platform: MBNXT (US only) or Legacy (EU/ANZ/UAE)


✔️ 4. Steps to Replicate (Most important)
Write like a recipe:

Log in as customer_id 98765


Go to the Products page


Add item to cart


Click Checkout


✔️ 5. Expected vs Actual Result
Expected: What should happen


Actual: What actually happened


✔️ 6. When & Frequency
Exact timestamp


Did it happen once? Every time? Randomly?


✔️ 7. Attachments
Screenshots or videos — Marker.io does this automatically.

❗ 4. What Are B2C Bugs vs B2B Bugs?

B2C Bugs (Customer-facing)
These appear on:

Groupon.com


Groupon mobile apps


Examples:

Broken button


Incorrect UI behavior


Page not displaying properly


⚠️ Important:
If the issue is about deal content (wrong price, missing fine print), 👉 It’s NOT a B2C bug — it’s a deal configuration issue → B2B bug.

B2B Bugs (Merchant-facing)
These appear on:

Merchant Center


Salesforce

image.png


Examples:

Merchant account not working


Booking settings are not saving


The Merchant Center features are not functioning


Always check if it’s:

Technical error → B2B bug


Human error (wrong data entered) → not a bug


🚨 5. What Is a GPROD Incident?


GPROD = serious production incident


Use GPROD when the issue:

Impacts ALL customers/merchants


Has a direct negative revenue impact


Breaks major functionality


Examples of GPROD incidents:
Website/app down


Payments failing


Orders are unable to be processed


Entire pages are not loading


GPROD Severity Levels:
Severity

Meaning

SEV 1

Critical – website down

SEV 2

Major issue, heavy impact

SEV 3

Moderate but important

SEV 4

Low impact but still revenue-related

SEV 5

Minor recurring issue affecting revenue



💬 6. How to Report a GPROD Incident

If you suspect a global issue: 👉 Ping @imoc immediately in Google Production Space.

IMOC will:

Review within 10 minutes


Validate if it’s an incident


Create a GPROD ticket


Start coordinating the resolution


Update regularly


IMOC is available:

Mon 00:00 UTC → Sat 00:00 UTC


On-call during weekends & global holidays


More info: gr.pn/issues

🛠️ 7. What Happens During a GPROD Incident

Once an incident is confirmed:

A dedicated Google Chat Space may be created


IMOC leads the investigation


Engineers join and work on the root cause


They’ll ask you for examples/logs if needed


Your role:
If someone tags you — respond fast and clearly. Avoid long chats or unclear replies. Every minute matters (incidents cost real revenue).

📄 8. After the Incident is Resolved


The incident ticket is updated


IMOC creates an Incident Review (IR) document


It’s assigned to the Service Owner


Engineering prepares action steps to prevent it from happening again


An IR meeting is scheduled


The end-to-end lifecycle is fully documented in internal resources.

🧭 9. Quick Decision Guide


Scenario

Report As

Minor issue affecting only one/few users

GBR bug

Incorrect deal info (price, fine print)

B2B issue

Bug in the Merchant Center or Salesforce

B2B GBR bug

Issue on Groupon.com/app

B2C GBR bug

Something is broken for ALL users

GPROD incident

Something impacting revenue

GPROD

You want maximum detail auto-captured

Use Marker.io

Here you can find a document with a full description: 

 👉GBR & GPROD: How to correctly report bugs and incidents
