title: CTSR: Reduce, Resolve, Prevent
details:
Org: CS ● LOB: All ● Region: All ●  Channel: All ● Requester: Adithya Venkateswaran

What's changing

Dispute status checks are no longer escalated to the CTSR team or SME by default (Except for PayPal dispute checks). CS agents will now perform the dispute status check themselves and escalate to SME/TL only if the issue cannot be resolved. The SME/TL decision tree has also been updated so it picks up from the point at which the agent escalates.

1. Summary of the Change
Ownership: Dispute status checks now sit with CS agents (previously escalated to CTSR/SME).

Escalation: Escalate to SME/TL only when the issue remains unresolved or the payment method requires it.

New decision tree location: Welcome → Fraud or Legal or Data privacy issue or Dispute → Dispute status check.

First branching question: “What is the form of payment?” — the path depends on the payment method used by the customer.

SME/TL DT updated: The SME/TL flow has been adjusted to pick up where the agent flow escalates. Most paths mirror the agent DT; “Groupon Won” now redirects to the Refund Exception path.

2. Why This Change
Empowering CS agents to handle dispute status checks directly:

Reduces handling time by removing unnecessary escalation hops.

Improves the customer experience with faster, first-contact resolution.

Keeps SME/TL bandwidth focused on genuinely unresolved or complex disputes.

3. Quick Reference
Payment Method

Action

Credit Card / Apple Pay

Agent checks dispute status in Adyen and follows the matching sub-path.

PayPal

Escalate to the CTSR team.

Klarna

Escalate to SME/TL to add to the Fraud Sheet; respond once the Fraud team provides a resolution.

Disputed value < 5 (CC/Apple Pay only)

Locate chargeback details. If found, follow the Adyen path; if not, escalate to SME/TL.

4. SOP — Step-by-Step Playbook
Step 1. Navigate the decision tree
Open the Welcome screen.

Select “Fraud or Legal or Data privacy issue or Dispute”.

Select “Dispute status check”.

When prompted “What is the form of payment?”, choose the option that matches the customer’s payment method.

Step 2. Follow the path for the customer’s payment method
A) Credit Card / Apple Pay — Check dispute status in Adyen
Look up the dispute in Adyen and follow the action that matches the dispute status:

Adyen Status

Agent Action

Under Review

Advise the customer to contact their financial institution for further assistance, as the dispute is still open.

Groupon WON the dispute

Assist the customer as per the normal refund policy.

Is the issue resolved?

Yes → No further action.

No → Escalate to SME/TL.

Groupon LOST the dispute

Was Bucks used to partially pay for this order?

Yes → Process the Bucks refund. Advise the customer that they have won the dispute and redirect them to their financial institution for the remaining OFP amount.

No → Do not process any refund. Advise the customer that they have won the dispute and redirect them to their financial institution for further assistance.

Customer says “Dispute Closed,” but Adyen shows “Dispute Unresolved.”

Escalate to TL/SME. Ask the TL/SME to add the issue to the Fraud Sheet to verify status; respond to the customer once the Fraud team provides the resolution.

B) PayPal — Escalate to CTSR
Escalate the issue to the CTSR team so the dispute status can be checked.

Templates to use: Dispute charges – Escalation to TL and Snippet – Dispute charges – Escalation to TL.

C) Klarna — Escalate to SME/TL
Escalate to the SME/TL and ask them to add the issue to the Fraud Sheet.

Respond to the customer once the Fraud team has provided the resolution.

D) Disputed Order value < 5 in Local Currency (Credit Card / Apple Pay only)
Ask yourself: “Were you able to locate the chargeback details?”

Yes → Follow the Adyen Dispute Status Check path (Section A).

No → Escalate to SME/TL to check the dispute status.

5. SME/TL Decision Tree
Why the SME/TL path is different

Because the agent DT only escalates to SME/TL when the issue is unresolved or the customer is unhappy with the dispute outcome, the SME/TL paths are now adjusted to pick up from that point — most paths mirror the agent DT, with a few specific overrides.

A) Credit Card / Apple Pay — SME/TL actions
Adyen Status

SME/TL Action

Under Review

Same actions as agent DT — advise the customer to contact their financial institution for further assistance, as the dispute is still open.

Groupon WON the dispute

Redirect to the Refund Exception path.

Rationale: The agent only escalates here when the issue is unresolved or the customer is unhappy with the dispute outcome, so the standard refund policy action has already been attempted.

Groupon LOST the dispute

Same actions as agent DT. Was Bucks used to partially pay this order?

Yes → Process the Bucks refund. Advise the customer that they have won the dispute and redirect them to their financial institution for the remaining OFP amount.

No → Do not process any refund. Advise the customer that they have won the dispute and redirect them to their financial institution for further assistance.

Customer says “Dispute Closed,” but Adyen shows “Dispute Unresolved.”

SME/TL adds the issue to the Fraud Sheet and responds to the customer once the Fraud team provides the resolution.

B) PayPal — SME/TL actions
Same actions as agent DT — escalate the issue to the CTSR team so the dispute status can be checked.

C) Klarna — SME/TL actions
SME/TL adds the issue to the Fraud Sheet and responds to the customer once the Fraud team provides the resolution.

D) Disputed Order value < 5 in Local Currency (Credit Card / Apple Pay only) — SME/TL actions
Were you able to locate the chargeback details?

Yes → Same actions as agent DT (follow the Adyen Dispute Status Check path in Section 5A).

No → SME/TL adds the issue to the Fraud Sheet and responds to the customer once the Fraud team provides the resolution.

6. Agent vs SME/TL — Side-by-Side Summary
Scenario

Agent Action

SME/TL Action

CC / Apple Pay — Under Review

Advise the customer to contact the financial institution.

Same as agent.

CC / Apple Pay — Groupon WON

Apply normal refund policy; escalate to SME/TL if unresolved.

Redirect to the Refund Exception path.

CC / Apple Pay — Groupon LOST

Check Bucks usage; refund Bucks if applicable; redirect customer to FI.

Same as agent.

Customer “closed” / Adyen “unresolved.”

Escalate to TL/SME → Fraud Sheet.

Add to Fraud Sheet; respond when Fraud team resolves.

PayPal

Escalate to the CTSR team.

Same as agent.

Klarna

Escalate to SME/TL → Fraud Sheet.

Add to Fraud Sheet; respond when Fraud team resolves.

Value < 5 — chargeback details located

Follow the Adyen path.

Same as agent.

Value < 5 — chargeback details NOT located

Escalate to SME/TL.

Add to Fraud Sheet; respond when Fraud team resolves.

7. Escalation Guide
Use this table to confirm where an escalation should go when one is required:

Scenario

Escalate To

PayPal dispute status check

CTSR team

Klarna dispute status check

SME/TL → Fraud Sheet

Adyen: Groupon won, but the issue is still unresolved for the customer

SME/TL

Customer says “dispute closed”, Adyen shows “unresolved.”

SME/TL → Fraud Sheet

Disputed value < 5 (CC/Apple Pay), and chargeback details cannot be located

SME/TL

8. Key Reminders
Always identify the payment method first — the entire path depends on it.

Only the Credit Card / Apple Pay path uses Adyen for the status check.

For Adyen “Groupon Lost” outcomes, check whether Bucks were used to partially pay before deciding on a refund action.

When in doubt, escalate to SME/TL — but only after the standard path does not resolve the issue.

title: Lekkerland iKiosk Gift Cards
details:
LOB: All ● Region: EMEA ● Channel: All ● Requester: Adithya Venkateswaran

Update

Status: New – for agent reference

This update introduces the Lekkerland iKiosk Gift Card for Germany customers and explains how to support customers who buy one at a kiosk and redeem it on Groupon.de. Redemption follows the existing Gift Card decision tree – no new tooling path is required.

What this update covers

What a Lekkerland iKiosk Gift Card is, and how customers buy one

The redemption process (account requirement + two redemption paths)

What to tell a customer who has lost their voucher

The existing Gift Card decision tree path agents must follow

Common issues, troubleshooting, and the refund policy

1.  What is a Lekkerland iKiosk Gift Card?

Lekkerland operates iKiosk points at selected retail locations. At these kiosks, customers can buy Groupon offers for local leisure activities – for example cinemas, zoos, or other attractions in their city.

After paying at the kiosk, the customer receives a printed gift voucher (printed as a greeting card or a paper receipt). The voucher carries a unique redemption code and short instructions. That code is what the customer redeems on Groupon.de to receive their offer or Groupon Bucks.

Which offers and prices are available depends on the kiosk – customers can see the current options on the promotional materials at the location and on the printed voucher itself.

2.  Redemption Process

Once the gift card is bought, the redemption process is the same as a standard Groupon Gift Card. There are two things every agent should know.

A Groupon account is required

The customer needs an existing Groupon account, or must create one (free, takes under a minute at groupon.de → Anmelden → Jetzt registrieren). Without an account the code cannot be used and the balance cannot be stored.

Two ways to redeem the code

Option A – Direct redemption (recommended)

Option B – Credit as Groupon Bucks

Best when the offer is still available.

Open the link printed on the voucher 

Add the offer to the cart and proceed to checkout.

Log in or create a free account if prompted.

Enter the code in the voucher / promo code field.

Total drops to €0 – a standard Groupon voucher is issued 

Best when the offer is no longer available, or the customer prefers credit.

Go to groupon.de/giftcards.

Log in or create a free account.

Enter the code and click “Einlösen” (Redeem).

The full value is credited as Groupon Bucks to the account.

Bucks can then be used on most eligible offers on Groupon.de.

Note on Groupon Bucks: Bucks can be used partially (the remainder stays in the account), and they expire on the same date printed on the voucher – advise the customer to redeem in time.

3.  Lost Voucher – What to Tell the Customer

Groupon cannot retrieve or reissue the code.

Codes issued on a physical voucher cannot be recovered by us. Ask the customer to contact the Lekkerland iKiosk location where they purchased the offer and request a copy of the voucher. There is no way for Support to look up or re-send a lost code.

4.  Decision Tree to Follow

For any Lekkerland iKiosk Gift Card query, follow the existing Gift Card decision tree. Select the path below in the tooling, then choose the relevant common issue at the end.

  Gifting  →  Gift Sender/Giftor  →  Recipient experiencing the issue with the Gift card redemption  →  Gift card  →  INTL  →  Groupon Gift Card with 22-characters Code, No PIN  →  [select the relevant common issue]  

Step 1  Gifting → Who is contacting us?

Confirm identity first. Select Gift Sender/Giftor.

Step 2  Gift Sender/Giftor → What is the exact issue?

Select “Recipient experiencing the issue with the Gift card redemption.”

Step 3  Gift card → Is it NAM or INTL?

For Lekkerland (Germany / groupon.de), select INTL.

Step 4  INTL → Which type of gift card?

Select “Groupon Gift Card with 22-characters Code, No PIN.” Use the ITOC templates on this node if needed.

Step 5  Groupon Gift Card → Common issues

Pick the matching issue: Issues with redeeming the Gift card, How to use a Gift Card, or Gift Card balance Inquiry.

5.  Common Issues & Troubleshooting

Situation

What to do

Code shows as invalid

Check the basics, in order:

Code entered correctly? Watch for look-alike characters (0 vs O, 1 vs I).

Has the expiry date on the voucher passed?

Has the code already been redeemed?

If all checks pass and it still fails, escalate in asana (see below).

Code shows as already used, but customer says they did not redeem it

Ask the customer to provide their voucher as proof, then escalate for investigation.

Offer is no longer available

Recommend redeeming the code as Groupon Bucks (Option B) and using the credit for an alternative offer on Groupon.de.

Escalation path

If a code still fails after the standard checks, or for the “already used” dispute, escalate to Nada Moravcikova or Linda Vavrikova. Always document the issue and the customer’s voucher details.

6.  Refunds & Cancellations

iKiosk purchases are non-refundable. Cancellations and refunds are not possible.

If the code is not redeemed before the expiry date on the voucher, it is no longer valid. Validity extensions and retroactive refunds are not possible – advise customers to redeem in time.

7.  Key Reminders

A Groupon account is mandatory for both redemption paths – customers can register for free during redemption.

Recommend Option A (direct) when the offer is still available; use Option B (Bucks) when it is not, or when the customer prefers credit.

Groupon Bucks expire on the voucher’s printed expiry date – remind the customer to redeem in time.

Lost voucher → Groupon cannot help. Direct the customer to the Lekkerland iKiosk location for a copy.

iKiosk purchases are non-refundable.

Follow the existing Gift Card DT path (INTL → 22-character code, No PIN). Don’t create a new path.

When in doubt, escalate to Nada Moravcikova or Linda Vavrikova.

Attachment

📎 Lekkerland iKiosk Gift Cards.pdf

Action Required

title: Fraud & Chargeback Communication Guidelines
details:
Update/Reminder

The Final Message for fraud-related and chargeback cases ensures clear, legally compliant, and operationally effective communication.


All communications must:

 ✅ Align with required actions, including scenarios where our fraud prevention vendor may provide chargeback defenses.

 ✅ Be consistent, legally compliant, and operationally effective.


Key principles:


The outcome and any funds involved are fully determined by the bank’s chargeback process.


Groupon has no influence once the bank completes its review.


Fraud-related or dispute information cannot be shared unless requested by law enforcement.


Saved payment details must be removed when fraud is detected.


Customer Communication DOs:

 ✅ Acknowledge the customer’s frustration.

 ✅ Explain that the dispute has been formally resolved by the bank.

 ✅ Confirm removal of saved payment details as a security measure.
Customer Communication DON’Ts:

 ❌ Do not confirm whether an order is fraudulent.

 ❌ Do not direct the customer to reopen a dispute already resolved in Groupon’s favor.

 ❌ Do not provide details of fraud team actions or investigation steps.

 ❌ Do not share transaction information such as IP, device, or other fraud-related data.
Example Response – Before Chargeback Final Status:
 "We understand this situation can be frustrating. Please note that the outcome of the transaction and any funds involved are determined entirely by your bank’s chargeback process. Groupon has no influence over this decision once the case is handled by the bank. If your bank confirms the transaction as valid, their decision is final, and we cannot change the outcome. For any further questions, we recommend contacting your bank directly. As a security measure, I'd like to confirm that the saved payment details have been removed."
Example Response – After Chargeback Final Status:
 "We understand this situation can be frustrating. Your bank has reviewed the case, confirmed the transaction as valid, and closed the dispute. Their decision is final, and Groupon has no authority to change the outcome or issue any credits after the bank has completed its review. For further questions about the review process, we recommend contacting your bank directly. As a security measure, I'd like to confirm that the saved payment details have been removed."

Action Required:

Always follow the DOs and DON’Ts when communicating about fraud or chargeback cases.


Do not disclose any details of the fraud investigation, dispute process, or transaction information unless requested by law enforcement.


Never proactively confirm fraud; responses should reflect the bank’s review and outcome.


Do not advise the customer to file a second dispute for a case already resolved in Groupon’s favor.


Remove saved payment methods when fraud is detected and confirm this to the customer.


Ensure all email and chat communications are consistent with these guidelines and legal requirements.

title: Process Update — Bucks Reinstatement for Reactivated Inactive Accounts — Effective Sep 21
details:
LOB: All ● Region: Global ● Channel: All ● Requester: Rajanandini Singhdeo

Update

Starting September 21, Groupon is launching an inactive-accounts program. Accounts that have been inactive for 30+ months will be deactivated, and any Groupon Bucks on those accounts will be voided at the time of deactivation.

Customer Notification (before deactivation)

Before the deactivation goes live, all affected Bucks-holding customers are receiving a one-time email notification informing them that their account will be deactivated on their communicated date and that their Groupon Bucks will be voided at that time.

Customers may reach out referencing this email. Please acknowledge the notification and follow the correct process based on the date (see below).

What happens from Sep 21

Customers will reactivate their own accounts by simply logging in with the same email (SSO or standard login). Reactivation is seamless — no agent action is needed to reactivate the account.

If a customer contacts us after logging back in and asks about their voided Bucks, agents will reinstate the Bucks in Cyclops using the new reason code "User Account Inactivity". Reinstated Bucks are valid for 180 days from the date of reissue.

Important: The CS Decision Tree already shows the new flow, there is not much difference in the current process and new process.

Quick Reference — Current vs. New

Area

Current Process

New Process

Account reactivation

Agent reactivates after email confirmation

Customer self-reactivates via login — no agent action

Bucks reinstatement

Reissue if voided

Reissue using reason code "User Account Inactivity"

Bucks validity

Standard

180 days from reissue

Decision Tree node

Reactivation Request for Inactive Account – with Inactive notes

Bucks Reinstatement for Inactive Account – with Inactive notes

Action Required — Until Sep 21

Before Sep 21, only notification emails are being sent out. Customers who received the notification may reach out saying they are unable to log in to their account.

Follow the existing DT path "Reset Password / Customer Unable to Login" to help the customer log back in.

Once the customer is able to log in successfully, no further action is needed.

Action Required — From Sep 21 Onwards (New Process)

When a customer contacts CS after logging back into a previously inactive account and asks about their Bucks:

Confirm the email address associated with the account.

Verify in Cyclops that the account is active.

Check the Cyclops Bucks history for a voided entry with description "User Account Inactivity" (voided amount and date will be visible).

Reissue the Bucks in Cyclops using reason code "User Account Inactivity" — valid for 180 days from reissue.

Confirm reinstatement with the customer and share the 180-day validity.

Template: SA.G19 – Reactivate Account (snippet updated)

Updated Snippet

I've reviewed your account and reinstated $XXX_BUCKS_CREDIT_XXX in Groupon Bucks, valid for 180 days from today.

As a goodwill gesture for the reactivation of your account, the Bucks have been reinstated.

Key Reminders

Affected customers have been notified in advance via email — acknowledge this if the customer references it.

Before Sep 21 → follow the Reset Password / Customer Unable to Login path.

From Sep 21 → customers self-reactivate via login; agents only reinstate Bucks.

Always use reason code "User Account Inactivity" when reissuing Bucks under the new flow.

Reinstated Bucks validity is 180 days and communicates this clearly to the customer.

title: DE Gifting — GrouponLive / Final Sale Vouchers
details:
LOB: All ● Region: EMEA ● Channel: All ● Requester: Adithya Venkateswaran

Update

What's changing

DE Final Sale / Live Events deals are now giftable. GrouponLive vouchers for fixed-date events remain non-refundable: they cannot be returned or exchanged, including when received as a gift. The gift recipient has exactly the same rights as the original purchaser — no more, no less.

1. Summary of the Change

Scope: DE market only, GrouponLive / Final Sale deals — tickets for live events with a fixed event date.

Position: Return, refund and exchange are excluded for these vouchers. This is a standard condition of the deal, not a case-by-case decision.

Gifting: Makes no difference to the outcome. The recipient inherits the purchaser’s rights in full — including the same restrictions.

One exception: If the event is cancelled, or rescheduled and the customer declines the new date, a refund IS due — gifted vouchers included.

Approved wording: Use the DE or EN reply template in Section 5 verbatim. Statutory references are deliberately left out of the customer reply, per Legal.

2. Why This Change

As we make DE Final Sale / Live Events deals giftable, CS needs one consistent line to follow:

Prevents customers being offered refunds or exchanges that do not apply to their deal.

Removes case-by-case interpretation, so every agent gives the same answer.

Avoids complaints and escalations on the DE market, which is particularly sensitive to refund and withdrawal-rights messaging.

Protects the genuine refund entitlement (cancelled / rescheduled events) by stating it explicitly rather than leaving it to the agent to remember.

3. When to Apply

Apply this guidance only when all three conditions below are true.

#

Condition

What to check

1

Market = DE

The order sits on the German site (groupon.de). This guidance does not apply to other markets.

2

Deal is marked Final Sale

The Fine Print marks the deal Final Sale / non-refundable / withdrawal excluded. In practice: GrouponLive tickets with a fixed event date.

3

Request is a return / refund / exchange on a gifted voucher

The customer asks to return, refund or exchange a voucher they gave as a gift or received as a gift.

If any one of the three is not met, do not use this guidance — follow the standard process for that deal type.

4. Agent SOP

When a customer asks to return, refund or exchange a gifted GrouponLive / Final Sale voucher:

Confirm the three conditions in Section 3 (DE market, Fine Print marks the deal Final Sale, request is a return / refund / exchange).

Check first whether the event has been cancelled or rescheduled. If it has, go straight to Section 7 — a refund is due and must not be denied.

If the event is going ahead as scheduled, send the approved reply from Section 5 in the customer’s language (DE or EN).

Point the customer to the GrouponLive refund-policy FAQ, which is already included as the closing line of both templates.

Close the contact. Do not offer a goodwill refund or credit as a workaround.

Important: The restriction comes from the fixed event date, not from the fact that the voucher was gifted. Never frame it as “because it was a gift.”

5. Approved Customer Responses

Copy and paste as-is. The wording was finalised in Legal review — do not paraphrase, shorten, or add statutory references.

5.1 Customer response — German (DE)

Vielen Dank für Ihre Nachricht. Bei diesem Angebot handelt es sich um ein GrouponLive-Ticket für eine Veranstaltung mit festem Termin. Das 14-tägige Widerrufsrecht gilt für dieses Angebot nicht. Die für Ihren Deal geltenden Bedingungen schließen daher Rückgabe und Umtausch aus. Dies gilt unabhängig davon, ob Sie das Ticket selbst gekauft oder als Geschenk erhalten haben – der Beschenkte hat dieselben Rechte wie der ursprüngliche Käufer. Eine Rückerstattung ist möglich, wenn die Veranstaltung abgesagt oder verschoben wird und Sie den Ersatztermin nicht wahrnehmen möchten. Weitere Informationen finden Sie hier: https://www.groupon.de/faq/grouponlive/grouponlive-ruckerstattungsrichtlinie-leitfaden-fur-ticket-ruckerstattungen

5.2 Customer response — English (EN)

Thank you for your message. This offer is a GrouponLive ticket for an event on a fixed date. The 14-day cancellation does not apply to this offer. Accordingly, the terms applicable to your deal exclude return and exchange. This applies regardless of whether you purchased the ticket yourself or received it as a gift – the gift recipient has the same rights as the original purchaser. A refund is possible if the event is cancelled or rescheduled and you do not wish to attend the replacement date. More information: https://www.groupon.de/faq/grouponlive/grouponlive-ruckerstattungsrichtlinie-leitfaden-fur-ticket-ruckerstattungen

6. Background for Agents

Internal context only — do NOT send any of this to the customer.

Fixed-date live event tickets: return, refund and exchange are excluded for this type of purchase. It is a standard condition of the deal, not a judgement call.

Gifting changes nothing. The recipient has the same rights as the original buyer — no more, no less.

Do not frame the restriction as “because it was gifted.” The reason is the fixed event date.

Statutory references were deliberately kept out of the customer-facing reply on Legal’s recommendation. Do not add them back in.

7. Exception — When the Refund IS Due

A refund applies, gifted vouchers included

If the event is cancelled, or is rescheduled and the customer does not wish to attend the replacement date, a refund is due. This applies to gifted vouchers exactly as it does to self-purchased ones, and must not be denied.

Situation

Outcome

Event going ahead on the scheduled date

No return, refund or exchange. Send the Section 5 reply.

Event cancelled

Refund applies — including gifted vouchers.

Event rescheduled and customer declines the new date

Refund applies — including gifted vouchers.

8. Do Not

Do not offer a goodwill refund or credit as a default workaround.

Do not tell the customer the restriction exists because the voucher was gifted — it is because of the fixed event date.

Do not apply this guidance to deals that are not marked Final Sale.

Do not deny a refund when the event has been cancelled or rescheduled and the customer declines the replacement date.

Do not paraphrase the approved reply or add statutory references to it.

9. Escalation

Unclear cases go to the DE CS lead. Escalate rather than improvise if:

It is not clear from the Fine Print whether the deal is Final Sale.

The customer disputes the restriction after receiving the approved reply.

The event status (cancelled / rescheduled / going ahead) cannot be confirmed.

The case involves a request the templates do not cover.

10. Key Reminders

All three conditions in Section 3 must be true before this guidance applies.

The gift recipient has the same rights as the original purchaser — no more, no less.

The reason for the restriction is always the fixed event date, never the gifting.

Cancelled or rescheduled events — refund applies, gifted vouchers included.

Use the DE / EN templates verbatim; both already close with the GrouponLive refund-policy FAQ link.

No goodwill refunds or credits as a default workaround.

11. Source & Sign-Off

Item

Detail

Wording finalised in

[LEGAL REVIEW] DE Gifting — Live Events (Final Sale) deals: confirm customer-facing wording [(Asana task)](https://app.asana.com/0/0/1216533882455384/f/)

Legal sign-off

Roberto Fiorenza, Legal

Statutory references

Deliberately excluded from the customer reply, per Legal’s recommendation.

Applies to

DE market — GrouponLive / Final Sale deals (fixed-date live events), including gifted vouchers.

Action Required

• Follow new CS guidance for DE Final Sale / Live Events giftable vouchers on returns, refunds, and exchanges.
• Confirm market (DE), deal (Final Sale), and request type (return/refund/exchange) before applying guidance.
• Prioritize refunds for cancelled or rescheduled-and-declined events; otherwise, send approved DE/EN reply verbatim, explaining fixed event date restrictions.
• Do not offer goodwill refunds or credits, and escalate complex cases to the DE CS lead.

title: ⏱️Delayed Refunds & Parked Cases Automation
details:
Overview


Cyclops now supports Delayed Refunds — a new functionality that allows agents to park a refund request for a defined period directly in Cyclops, without the need to create a case in Salesforce (SF). Once the delay period expires, the system will automatically verify the order status and process the refund only if the order has not been redeemed.


Before (Old Process)

Now (New Process)

● Create a case in Salesforce to park the refund

● Monitor the case manually until the delay period ends

● Manual verification and processing required

● Set the delay directly in Cyclops — no SF case needed

● System auto-verifies order status after the delay period

● Refund processed automatically for unredeemed orders


🖥️ How to Set a Delayed Refund in Cyclops


Steps to Apply a Delayed Refund

1.  Open the order in Cyclops and navigate to the Decrease Quantity option.

2.  Locate the Delay Refund checkbox and tick it:image.png

3.  An input field will appear next to the checkbox. Enter the number of days for the delay (must be greater than 0).

4.  Submit. The refund request will be stored and will NOT be processed in real time.

5.  A pending refund indicator will be visible on the voucher in both the voucher details view and the DecreaseQuantity modal.

Screenshot 2026-01-29 at 6.51.17 PM.png


💡 TIP:  The standard delay period is 48 hours. Use the Decision Tree to confirm if a different delay period applies to your case type.


⚠ IMPORTANT:  The delay field requires a value greater than 0 days. Always refer to the Decision Tree to confirm the appropriate delay period before submitting.


🔄 After the Delay Period: What Happens Next?


Once the delay period has elapsed, Cyclops will automatically verify the order status:

Order Status

Outcome

✅  Not Redeemed

Refund is processed automatically. Customer will receive a notification and will see the order refunded in their account. 

No further action required from the agent. Customer does not need to contact us again.

⚠️  Redeemed

Refund is NOT automatically processed. Agent must follow the Redeemed Order protocol (see Section 4 below) before refund can be issued.


📩 Customer Communication Template


Use the template below when contacting a customer whose order was found to be redeemed after the delay period.

📧  Customer Message Template — Redeemed Order

Thank you for your patience. We are currently reviewing your refund request for order [Order Number].

Before we can process the refund, we need to confirm with the merchant that the voucher code has been deactivated in their system. This process can take up to XX hours.

Once the refund has been approved, you will receive a notification and the refunded amount will be visible in your account. You do not need to contact us again — we will update you automatically.

⚠️ Please note: If the voucher is used with the merchant during this period, the refund will not be processed.

We appreciate your understanding.


Note for CS: Please use the parking option in Salted only for merchants like Adidas and Costco, as these require additional checks. For all other merchants, like ZRK merchants, if no further validation is needed beyond checking the redemption status, the parking option in Salted is not necessary. In such cases, the request can be directly added to Cyclops under delayed refunds.

📌 Quick Reference Summary


Topic

Key Point

SF Case Required?

No — delay is set directly in Cyclops

Standard Delay Period

48 hours (confirm with Decision Tree for exceptions)

Unredeemed After Delay

Refund processed automatically — no agent action needed

Redeemed After Delay

The agent must action in Cyclops + follow Redeemed Order protocol + use the approved customer template

Customer Notification

Auto-sent once refund approved — customer does not need to follow up

Voucher Used During Review

Refund WILL NOT be processed
keywords: ⏱️Delayed Refunds & Parked Cases Automation

title: Clear Communication on Discretionary Exceptions
details:
Org: CS ● LOB: All ● Region: Global ●  Channel: All

Update

In scenarios such as purchase by mistake, expired vouchers, or credit reinstatement requests, the decision tree explicitly authorizes Groupon Bucks as a goodwill exception for selected Hival / Super Hival / New customers, even when the purchase does not qualify for a refund under the Terms & Conditions.

When interacting with customers, our responses do not consistently clarify that this is a discretionary, one-time exception.

Going forward, communication should clearly state the gesture as a one-time exception while maintaining a professional, policy-aligned tone.

Action Required

1️⃣ Clearly Reference Policy First: Begin by confirming that the purchase does not qualify under the Terms & Conditions or refund policy. Maintain a neutral and factual tone.

2️⃣ Make the Exception Explicit: Clearly state that the credit is a one-time exception based on the customer’s purchase history or continued business.

3️⃣ Maintain the Correct Tone: Show appreciation for the customer’s loyalty without over-apologizing. Do not suggest it is unfair or create expectations of repeated exceptions.

The following examples model how to reference policy while clearly positioning the credit as a discretionary, one-time exception. The goal is to protect policy integrity while acknowledging customer value.

“As per our Terms & Conditions, this purchase isn’t eligible for a refund. Given your regular purchases with us however, I’ve made a one-time exception and credited your account with Groupon Bucks.”

“Under our Terms & Conditions, this isn’t refundable. That said, I can see you’ve been ordering with us consistently, so I’ve added Groupon Bucks to your account as a one-time exception.”

“As outlined in our Terms & Conditions, this deal doesn’t qualify for a refund. Considering your history with us, I’ve issued Groupon Bucks as a one-time exception.”

“According to our policy, this purchase isn’t eligible for a refund. Taking your past purchases into account, however, I’ve made an exception and added credit to your account.”

“This falls outside our refund policy. However, based on your purchase history with us, I’ve approved a one-time exception and added Groupon Bucks to your account.”

“As stated in our Terms & Conditions, we’re unable to process a refund for this purchase. Given your continued business with us, I’ve added Groupon Bucks as a one-time gesture.”

All iPhone orders above 250 value are placed in “Pending” status

The Fraud team reviews these orders within 24 hours 

After review, orders are either approved or cancelled due to fraud

Reviews are typically completed before 5 PM CEST

Inform the customer that any authorized funds will be released within 10 business days

Customer wants to proceed with the order:

Advise the customer to wait up to 24 hours for the order to move to the shipping stage

If Order is Already Processed: 

Inform the customer that the order has been successfully processed

Important Note: 
Always check the order status in Cyclops or in CI before taking any action

Orders may remain in Pending for up to 24 hours due to fraud review

title: Updated Chat Closure Protocol
details:
Org: CS ● LOB: All ● Region: All ●  Channel: Chat ● Requester: Nithya Subramani

Update

We will be implementing an updated chat resolution approach effective immediately to improve efficiency, customer experience, and overall contact resolution performance.

Scenario: Issue Resolved – Customer Acknowledged

When the customer’s issue has been fully resolved, and the customer acknowledges the resolution either explicitly or implicitly (for example: “Thanks,” “Got it,” “That worked,” etc.), agents are no longer required to ask additional closing questions such as:

➡️“Is there anything else I can help you with?”
➡️“Do you have any other concerns today?”
➡️"Please let me know if you have any further questions."
Instead, agents should:
➡️Provide a warm and professional closing message
➡️Resolve the chat immediately
➡️Move on to the next customer interaction

Example
Customer: “Thanks for fixing that!”
Agent: “You’re welcome! Thanks for contacting Groupon! Have a great day!”
→ Resolve the conversation using the appropriate outcome selection.

title: Updated SET Escalation Process
details:
Org: CS ● LOB: All ● Region: All ●  Channel: All ● Requester: Adithya Venkateswaran

What’s Changing?
We’re updating the process for handling Legal / Social Media threats to provide clearer guidance on:
✅ When to resolve issues within the team
✅ When to escalate to CTSR
✅ How to identify if legal/external action is already in progress
✅ Handling self-harm or life-threatening statements
✅ Applying a new severity-based remedy approach for threats without action
Key updates
1️⃣ Don’t default to CTSR
If the issue can be resolved within standard policy or corrected in-team, resolve it directly — no escalation needed.
Examples:
✔ First-time issue resolved within policy → Handle & resolve
✔ Previous process not followed correctly → Correct and resolve
2️⃣ Identify whether legal/external action is already in progress
Escalate to CTSR if customers provide evidence such as:
• BBB complaint already filed
• Attorney involvement
• Police report reference
• Bank dispute initiated
• Demand letter/summons / legal correspondence
➡ These indicate action already in progress
Examples:
“I have filed a BBB complaint.”
“My attorney is preparing documentation.”
Outcome: Escalate to CTSR
3️⃣ Threats ≠ Action
Statements like:
• “I will sue.”
• “I’ll post on Facebook.”
• “I’ll dispute the charge.”
These indicate intent only, not action already taken.
➡ Continue with severity assessment instead of escalating immediately.
4️⃣ New escalation path for self-harm or life-threatening concerns
If a customer:
• Threatens self-harm
• Reports life-threatening risk
➡ Escalate to Fraud/Risk immediately
❌ Do NOT escalate to CTSR
❌ Do NOT apply severity remedies
5️⃣ New severity-based remedy approach (Threat/Intent only)
High severity → Offer a full refund in Bucks (exception)
Medium severity → Offer 10% of the order value in Bucks
Low severity → Reiterate resolution & close case
Quick reference
Situation
Action
Issue resolved within policy
Resolve in-team
The previous process was not followed correctly
Correct & resolve
Legal/external action already initiated
Escalate to CTSR
Self-harm / life-threatening statements
Escalate to Fraud/Risk
Threat only (“I will…”)
Apply severity assessment

Reminder 💡
Always document the exact customer wording or signal observed when escalating to CTSR or Fraud/Risk.

title: Merchant Issue Handling (Refund First Approach)
details:
Org: CS & MO ● LOB: All ● Region: Global ●  Channel: All

Update

As a further improvement to reduce avoidable escalations and improve customer experience, the next course of action has been clarified for Merchant Issue cases. 

We want to give customers their money back faster without making them wait for a second team to look at the case. This reduces "back-and-forth" and lets Merchant Operations focus on investigating bad merchants rather than just clicking "approve" on refunds.

Action Required

When you confirm a Merchant Issue using the Zingtree checklist, you should now process the refund yourself (if eligible) before escalating. Do not wait for Merchant Operations (MO) approval to give the customer their money back.

Check: Use the mandatory Zingtree checklist (Google status, reviews, merchant site, and Cyclops).

Verify: If the evidence confirms the merchant is at fault:

For Unredeemed/Expired Vouchers: Process the refund immediately in the tool.

For Partial Service Issues: Process the refund in Bucks.

Document: Add your findings clearly in Salted CX.

Escalate: Send the case to MO after the refund is done so they can DNR (Do Not Re-feature) the merchant or pause the deal.

Exception: For Redeemed Vouchers in the INTL region, do NOT refund. Escalate these to MO for verification first.

Key Concepts to Master:

Mandatory Evidence: Agents must check five specific sources (Google, Reviews, Merchant Website, Fine Print, and Cyclops) before taking action.

Sequential Workflow: The shift from "Escalate-then-Refund" to "Refund-then-Escalate."

Tool Competency: Full ownership of the refund process within Salted CX for expired and cooling-off cases.

Regional Specificity: Understanding that the INTL region has a different workflow for redeemed vouchers.

The "Danger Zone" (Confusion Risks):

INTL Redeemed Vouchers: Agents might get into a "flow" of refunding everything and accidentally refund an INTL redeemed voucher. This requires a hard stop.

Incomplete Documentation: MO will reject escalations if the checklist isn't visible in the chat/notes. Agents may skip steps to improve handle time.

Partial Service: Agents may struggle to decide between a cash refund and Bucks. The policy is strictly Bucks for partial service issues.

Scenario Examples:

Correct Handling: A customer reports a merchant is closed. The agent checks Google (shows "Permanently Closed") and recent reviews (confirming closure). The agent processes a refund for the expired voucher immediately, notes the evidence in Salted CX, and then escalates to MO to pause the deal.

Incorrect Handling: A customer in the INTL region says their voucher was redeemed by mistake. The agent confirms the merchant issue via the checklist and processes a refund to the customer's credit card. (Error: Redeemed INTL vouchers must always be escalated to MO first without a CS refund).

title: AI Chatbot Launch – Rollout & Agent Guidelines
details:
Update:
We’re excited to announce the launch of our new AI Chatbot, designed to streamline support by handling initial customer queries and freeing agents to focus on complex issues.
Starting Thursday, 31 July 2025, the chatbot will be rolled out to 5–10% of customers, who will see both existing self-service options and a new chat widget.

💡How It Works:
The chatbot manages first-contact queries and automatically creates a Salesforce case that includes the following details:


Full transcript (with English translation).


Auto-populated customer/order details.


A subject line summarizing the interaction.
🤖 Chatbot Coverage Includes:
Refunds for local deals, expired or refunded vouchers (credit, cash, or mixed payments) - including North America, international orders, including country-specific refund policies (e.g., Germany, Netherlands).


Redemption issues, including merchant concerns, booking assistance, and coded deal problems.


Merchant Issue inquiries, where the chatbot reads active memos to share informative updates or initiate refunds.


If a memo is marked under investigation, the bot will create a Salesforce case and assign it to the agent.


Status checks (failed, rejected, pending, held orders).


🔺 Outside Chatbot Scope – Agent Handling Required:
Anything outside the above (e.g., gifted vouchers or gift-related queries, lobs except local, redeemed vouchers, high-risk issues) is transferred to an agent.


📩 Customer Communication:
The chatbot will inform customers that their request will be addressed within 24 hours by the agent.


📁 Audit Trail:
Full customer-chatbot conversation saved in Salesforce for transparency.

Action Required:
Review the Transcript


Always read the full chatbot-customer conversation to understand the request fully.


Verify Contact Category


The chatbot assigns a contact category - review and update if incorrect.


Process Refunds Directly


If the chatbot has approved a refund:


Issue it directly to the customer’s selected method (e.g., original payment method or Bucks).
Do not send an SSR link for these cases.


Send Refund Confirmation Emails


Although system emails are sent, always send a manual refund confirmation email to ensure the customer is informed (automated emails can go to spam).
❓ Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
Q: Does the chatbot only handle refunds?
 A: No. It also manages redemption issues, Merchant issue queries via memos, voucher refunds, and status checks. See Chatbot Coverage section above.
Q: Do I still need to email the customer if the bot approved a refund?
 A: Yes. Send a manual confirmation email to avoid spam filter issues.
Q: What if the chatbot wrongly approves a refund (e.g., for a final sale item)?
 A: If due to a setup/system error (e.g., final sale not marked), the refund must be honored, and flag it immediately. This is similar to how Zingtree errors are handled.
Q: Can customers reopen a chatbot session?
 A: No. Each interaction is new and creates a separate case.
Q: Does the chatbot handle reopened cases?
 A: No. It doesn’t check for case history and treats every session as new.
Q: Should I change the contact category selected by the chatbot?
 A: Yes. Always review and correct if it’s not accurate.
Q: Does the chatbot offer 10% extra credit or generate SSR links?
 A: No. The chatbot does not offer extra credits or send SSR links. Agents must not use SSR links for these cases.
Q: What happens if a customer asks about an issue already linked to an open memo?
A: The chatbot will create a new case and link it to the memo if applicable and will be transferred to an agent. However, it does not review past case history.

Promo codes must always be communicated as offering “up to X% off”, as the final discount applied can vary based on deal eligibility and conditions.

Key Reminder:

Promo codes provide up to the stated percentage (e.g., up to 10% off)


The actual discount may range from 1% up to the maximum percentage


A specific discount amount or percentage must not be guaranteed

If a promo code offers up to 10% off, the customer may receive any discount between 1% and 10%, depending on the deal. Receiving a lower percentage (for example, 3%) is still within the eligible range.

Do not promise or imply a guaranteed discount percentage


Use only the approved promo code snippet when offering promo codes:

“We’re sorry for the inconvenience caused and would like to offer you an exclusive promo code to enhance your Groupon experience with great discounts on your next purchase.

Your code: XXXXXXXX – Get up to 20% off on eligible local deals, with a maximum discount of $50 per voucher.

Rule

title: ARAL eSuperCard Launch – Germany
details:
Org: CS ● LOB: All ● Region: DE ●  Channel: All

Update

We are launching a new deal in Germany: the ARAL eSuperCard (€40 paid = €42 value).

Please review the below process carefully to ensure accurate case handling and consistent customer communication.

🛒 How the Deal Works (Customer Journey)
Customer purchases the voucher on Groupon.

Within 14 days of purchase → Voucher is not redeemed. Refunds are allowed.

After 14 days → Voucher is automatically marked as redeemed (order details are shared with ARAL).
 ❌ No refunds allowed after this point.

The ARAL eSuperCard is issued directly by ARAL and sent via email.

Delivery timeframe: Up to 30 days from purchase date
 (14-day cooling-off period + ARAL processing time).

⚠️ The card is sent to the email address entered during checkout, which may differ from the customer’s account email.

🔄 What Is Changing?
We are introducing a new third-party issued voucher (ARAL eSuperCard) in Germany. The voucher will now automatically move to redeemed status after 14 days from purchase, and refunds will no longer be possible once this happens. Additionally, card issuance is fully managed by ARAL and delivered directly to the checkout email provided by the customer.

🎯 Why Is This Happening?
This process aligns with ARAL’s fulfillment structure and ensures compliance with the 14-day cooling-off regulation. It also clearly defines responsibility: Groupon manages the sale and refund window, while ARAL manages card issuance and usage. This ensures transparency, operational clarity, and consistent customer communication.


Action Required

Refund requested within 14 days of purchase
Approve the refund, as the voucher is still unredeemed.

Refund requested after 14 days of purchase
Decline the refund. The voucher has been automatically redeemed and no exceptions apply. Refer the customer to the Deal Conditions.

Customer asking where their card is (within 30 days of purchase)
Advise the customer that the ARAL eSuperCard can take up to 30 days from the purchase date to be issued. Ask them to check their spam or junk folder and confirm the timeframe has not yet passed.

Suggested response:

“Thank you for reaching out. As mentioned in the deal conditions, your ARAL eSuperCard can take up to 30 days from the purchase date to be issued by ARAL. It will be sent to the email address provided at the time of purchase. If the 30-day timeframe has not yet passed, we kindly ask for your patience. In the meantime, please check your spam or junk folder.”

Customer has not received the card after 30 days
Escalate to MO after confirming the customer has checked their spam/junk folder. Inform the customer that the case has been escalated to ARAL for investigation and that an update will be shared once received.

Suggested response:

“Hi {{dc.api-first_name}}, I'm sorry to hear that you haven't received your card. Please make sure you have checked your spam or junk folder. As more than 30 days have passed since your purchase, we are now escalating your case to ARAL for investigation. We have shared your details with them and will update you as soon as we receive their response.”

Customer reports an issue using the card at a gas station
Redirect the customer to ARAL Customer Service, as ARAL manages issuance and redemption issues directly.

Suggested response:

“I'm sorry to hear that you experienced an issue when trying to use your ARAL eSuperCard. As the card is issued and managed directly by ARAL, they are best placed to investigate redemption issues at the station. We recommend contacting ARAL Customer Service for immediate support. If helpful, please let us know what error message or situation occurred, and we can share the details with ARAL to assist further.”

Customer does not know which email was added during purchase or entered an incorrect email
Check the email address entered at checkout in Cyclops. You will be able to view the information provided during purchase and edit it if applicable.

title: McDonald's Campaign — Agent Guideline
details:
Org: CS ● LOB: All ● Region: NAm ●  Channel: All ● Requester: Samuel Garcia Rio 

What is it?

McDonald's app users receive a single-use promo code worth 30% off eligible Local deals

Campaign runs May 7 – July 31, 2026

Peak volume expected May 7 – May 17

Customers land on groupon.com/landing/mcdonalds

When to Use

When a customer reaches out saying the code didn't apply, the discount was smaller than expected, or they can't use it on a deal they wanted.

Key Terms

Eligible deals: ~85% of Local deals can absorb the margin, and these get the full 30% off

Excluded deals: ~15% of Local deals (the most popular, high-demand ones, e.g., Costco, Sam's Club, Chuck-e-cheese) plus all Viator, Goods, and Travel.

McDonald 's-promo customer: Anyone mentioning McDonald's, arriving from the landing page, or matching the code pattern.

How to Identify a McDonald's Promo Customer

Customer mentions McDonald's or the McDo app

They arrived from groupon.com/landing/mcdonalds

Promo code matches the McDonald's code pattern (14-character promo code, with no 0/O and 1/I )

Agent Talk Track

Use this when a McDonald's customer says the code didn't work:

"Thanks for reaching out — I can see why that's confusing. The McDonald's offer is 30% off, but it only applies to eligible Local deals. The deal you picked isn't on the list."

Then explain: The code applies to most Local deals, but a subset of popular deals, plus Viator, Goods, and Travel are excluded. Not a bug, additional discounts are not eligible for these deals.

Goodwill Remedy

Issue $5 Groupon Bucks as a one-time welcome credit if:

Customer is confirmed as McDonald 's-promo (code redemption attempt verified in history)

Frustrated that they can't use it on their chosen deal

Important Safeguards

One per customer: Do not add more than one time goodwill credit per customer

Must verify redemption attempt, confirm that customer tried to use it and has not worked, do not apply goodwill credit if customer used the McDonald's discount.

Tag as MCDO-GOODWILL-2026. When you add the goodwill credit in Cyclops, add this in the comment, so we can track volume and measure.

Escalation Path

Tier 1 (You): Issue $5 goodwill if all safeguards are met

Tier 2 (Manager): Customer dispute unresolved? Escalate to the CS supervisor. Do not issue larger credits without manager sign-off

Sponsor: In case of a big increase in volume of requests, flag it to Ernest or Samu. 

Quick FAQs

Q: Does every deal get 30% off?

A: No. Most (~85%) do, but the popular, high-demand ones (~15%) are excluded. That's why the customers can be frustrated.

Q: What if they try to use it on Viator or Travel?

A: The code is Core Local-only. Viator, Goods, and Travel are not eligible.

Q: Can I give them a bigger credit?

A: Not without manager approval. Stick to $5 unless escalated.

Q: What if they say they're not a McDonald's customer?

A: Don't issue goodwill. They're regular promo customers and follow the regular policy.

title: SET Escalation Protocol
details:
LOB: All ● Region: Global ●  Channel: All ● Requester: Deepa Lakshmi Maniam
We’ve observed that some cases are being incorrectly escalated to the SET queue as customer threats when they do not qualify. This update clarifies when and how to use the SET escalation protocol.
A threat is defined as any explicit statement from a customer indicating intent to take formal action against the company, including:
Mentions of legal action, lawsuits, solicitors, or attorneys
References to regulatory bodies (e.g., ASA, OFT, Trading Standards, BBB)
Threats to escalate publicly via social media, press, or review platforms
It is important to note that the SET team does not handle customer issues. Escalation to SET is for audit/FYI purposes only, and not for resolution.


If a customer makes a threat, agents must continue to handle and resolve the issue from their end. Do not inform the customer about SET escalation.
Escalate to SET only when:
The customer makes a legal, regulatory, BBB, or social media threat
Do NOT escalate to SET when:
The customer asks for a corporate address → provide details from the Decision Tree
The customer is dissatisfied or requests escalation → handle via SME/TL
The customer mentions bank disputes or chargebacks
The case requires escalation to another team (MO/other team)
In scenarios where a threat is mentioned but the case needs to be escalated to another team:
Add an internal note about the threat (mandatory)
Proceed with the relevant team escalation (MO/other team)
Do not escalate to SET, as the issue is still being handled
Legal Contact Handling
If a legal team contacts on behalf of a customer:
NAm: Direct them to send communication to the registered agent in Illinois
INTL (do not share with customers):
For regulatory/transactional data requests (order history, refunds, chargebacks, payment method, etc.) → escalate to the relevant policereports@groupon.xx email
For other legal requests → escalate to the Legal team

title: Gender-Inclusive SOP
details:
Org: CS ● LOB: All ● Region: All ●  Channel: All ● Requester: Ernest Dulnik 

Update

Groupon has introduced a Gender-Inclusive Deal Language & Anti-Discrimination Standards SOP https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ULrNf2cHT7b6YFYPxoBrB0fTZNZhbwlo66no2CrWEn8/edit?tab=t.0. As Customer Service agents, you may encounter customers who have been denied a service by a merchant on the basis of their gender, or you may notice gender-based eligibility language when reviewing deal details during a contact. This communication gives you clear guidance on how to recognize these situations, what to say to the customer, and when to escalate.
Gender-based eligibility restrictions — such as "women only" or "men only" — are not permitted on Groupon deals unless they are inherent to the nature of the service (e.g., a prostate exam or an OBGYN consultation). If a merchant refuses a customer on this basis for a general service, that is a discrimination complaint and must be handled accordingly.

Action Required

When a customer contacts you about a gender-related service denial
Acknowledge the customer's experience with empathy — do not dismiss or minimise their concern.
Use the ready-to-use customer response template in the SOP to ensure consistent, compliant language in your reply.
Process a refund or resolution for the customer as appropriate while the complaint is being escalated.
Recognising the difference: allowed vs. not allowed
Allowed: Services where the treatment is tied to specific anatomy — e.g., OBGYN exams, prostate checks, or gendered service descriptors like "Women's Brazilian Wax" or "Men's Haircut." These describe what the service is, not who is allowed.
Not allowed: Merchant-imposed restrictions for general services — phrases like "women only," "men only," "ladies only," or "reserved for [gender]." These are instances of discrimination and should be treated as a complaint.
If you are unsure whether a restriction is inherent to the service or merchant-imposed, escalate. Do not make a judgment call on your own.
When a general contact becomes a discrimination complaint
Some contacts may start as a standard voucher-not-honored inquiry and reveal a gender-based refusal during the conversation. Treat this as a discrimination complaint from that point forward.
Escalate to Legal/Risk as directed in the SOP — do not attempt to resolve the merchant side of the complaint yourself.
Escalation path
Use the customer response template from the SOP to communicate with the customer.
Flag the case to your Team Lead, noting that it is a gender-based discrimination complaint.
Your Team Lead will pass the case to Legal/Risk per the SOP escalation process.
Document all relevant details of the contact clearly in the case notes before escalating.

details:
Org: CS ●  LOB: All ● Region: Global ●  Channel: All 
This update clarifies how to handle refund requests when the Chatbot processes a refund for only one voucher instead of multiple vouchers within the same order.

When a customer initially contacts us to request a refund for multiple vouchers in one order, the Chatbot may process a refund for only one voucher.

If the customer contacts us again regarding the remaining vouchers, consider the original contact date as the refund request date (i.e., the date when the first voucher was refunded by the Chatbot).

Example:
Customer contacts us on 7 February (within the cancellation window) requesting a refund for an order with three vouchers.

The Chatbot refunds only one voucher.

The customer contacts us again on 12 February (now outside the cancellation window) regarding the remaining vouchers.

The refund request date must still be considered as 7 February (within the cancellation window).

Note:
 This applies only to cases where the Chatbot missed refunding multiple vouchers within the same order.

title: Salesforce Messaging and Survey Improvements
details:
Update

This update outlines key changes aimed at streamlining the customer support experience through Salesforce Messaging. These updates are designed to optimize workflows, improve chat accessibility, enhance the visibility of issue descriptions, and expand survey feedback collection. The ultimate goal is to boost operational efficiency, reduce customer effort, and increase engagement and satisfaction.

Inactive Chat – Important Update 
Agents are currently not marking chats as inactive, which impacts tracking and feedback collection. To address this, a new SOP for Salesforce Messaging (CS Team) is created.

1. Elimination of Redundant Pre-Chat Formalities
To streamline the customer support journey, redundant pre-chat forms will be removed for logged-in users. Since customer data and issue details are already captured through the Zingtree workflow and transferred between systems, these forms no longer provide added value. The feasibility of extending this improvement to non-logged-in users will also be assessed, ensuring a seamless support experience while mitigating risks associated with maintaining two separate experiences.

2. Instant Chat Initiation
Chats initiated via Zingtree will now instantly connect users with an available agent, eliminating unnecessary delays or extra steps. This enhancement ensures a faster, more responsive support experience.

3. Enhanced Issue Description Visibility in Chat
Currently, customer-reported issue details are stored in the case but aren’t visible within the chat window. To improve transparency and agent efficiency, these details will now be included in the automated chat initiation message. If the description exceeds a set character limit, it will be truncated while preserving the core information. This message will also follow a standardized template that welcomes the customer, confirms their queue status, and sets expectations around agent assignment.
4. Persistent Chat Accessibility Throughout the FAQ Ecosystem
 Currently, chat is only accessible on the specific FAQ end-node page where it was initiated. If a customer navigates away, the session disappears, requiring them to return to the end-node to re-engage. The new implementation will ensure that both active and inactive chats remain visible across the entire FAQ ecosystem, reducing customer effort and improving engagement.
Once a chat is officially closed, one of the following will occur:
The chat will disappear entirely from the FAQ.


The chat will remain visible but locked—allowing only survey completion—and prompt the customer to restart the Zingtree workflow for any new inquiries.


5. Expanding Survey Coverage for Inactive Chats
 Currently, surveys are only triggered for chats that are formally ended, which limits feedback collection—especially since many sessions close due to inactivity. To address this, surveys will now also be sent for inactive chats.
To reduce potential dissatisfaction and confusion:
The survey page will retain the visual illusion of an active chat in the background.


A "Back to Chat" button will allow customers to re-engage before completing the survey.


The survey will clearly differentiate between inactive chats and resolved cases to set proper expectations.


6. Embedding Surveys in Email Correspondence
 Currently, CSAT surveys are sent as separate emails, often arriving before resolution details—leading to potential confusion and lower ratings. Going forward, CSAT surveys will be embedded directly in the footer of every support email. This ensures feedback is collected in context, improving both accuracy and response rates.
The embedded survey will:
Focus on agent performance with a direct satisfaction question.


Automatically record the selected rating upon interaction.


Redirect customers to the full survey page for additional comments or insights.


7. Storing Multiple Survey Responses with Channel Attribution
 With the expanded survey strategy, multiple feedback instances will now be recorded at the case level, with each response attributed to its originating channel—be it an ended chat, inactive chat, or email interaction.
This allows for more comprehensive tracking and enables deeper, data-driven insights into customer sentiment and service performance across all digital support channels.
Strategic Impact
 These enhancements are designed to create a more efficient and user-friendly support experience by reducing customer effort, boosting engagement, and improving the accuracy of feedback. By optimizing Salesforce Messaging and survey processes, the organization will not only elevate service quality but also refine operational workflows—driving greater alignment with evolving customer expectations.
Action Required
Expect chats to start instantly without pre-chat forms for logged-in users. No extra steps from the customer side.


Be prepared to respond immediately once a chat connects—there won’t be a delay or form submission beforehand.


Make sure to read the initial chat message carefully—it now includes the customer’s issue details pulled from Zingtree.


Please know that customers can now access their chat across all FAQ pages—not just where it started. This helps reduce effort and keeps the conversation going.
Once a chat ends:
It will either disappear, or
Stay visible but locked for survey only, prompting a restart for new queries.
Be aware so you can guide customers as needed!
Use the “Customer Inactive” option when a customer hasn’t responded.


This will trigger an automated message: “Chat paused due to inactivity.”


It will also show the survey form to the customer.


Get familiar with how inactive chat surveys will appear—they’ll look like an active chat with a “Back to Chat” button.


Be mindful that CSAT surveys are now embedded in email footers. Customers might rate their experience as they read your message—so keep replies clear, helpful, and complete.


Remember that feedback will be recorded for every channel (ended chats, inactive chats, and emails).


Follow the SOP for handling inactive chats in Salesforce Messaging.

title: Gifting CSAT Snapshot: Turning April’s Dip Into a Win
details:
What’s this about?
After a strong start to the year, April was a tough month for Gifting, with CSAT dipping by -8% compared to March. While many DSATs were outside our control, ~18% were not, and that’s where we’re focusing our efforts. The good news? Mother’s Day sparked a strong comeback, with record-high Gift Orders and CSAT climbing back to 77% in Week 2 of May. Let’s keep building on that momentum! 💪



 Mother’s Day Magic!
Our 2025 Mother’s Day week was a standout success! We saw the highest number of Gift Orders this year — 101,223 orders, marking a +17.3% increase compared to Mother’s Day week in 2024 (86,320 orders).


This surge in gifting activity also led to more customer engagements, but what’s worth celebrating is that our CSAT held strong and even showed an upward trend from the first week of May, proving that we delivered under pressure. 💪

Gifting Performance so far


In April, Gifting CSAT dropped by -8% compared to March, hitting 73%, one of the lowest scores of the year and on par with January, despite fewer surveys.


CSAT analysis revealed that ~18% of DSATs were controllable, giving us a clear opportunity to improve.


🌼 Turning It Around in May:
Thanks to your continued focus and care in handling gift-related contacts, we saw CSAT bounce back starting the first week of May.


Week 2 of May (Mother’s Day week) hit 77% CSAT, showing a strong recovery, even with increased survey volume and engagements.
Gifting Lessons in Focus


Over the past few weeks, we’ve reviewed Gifting-related DSATs to understand better where things are going off track. While a majority of issues stem from factors outside our control, we’ve identified several recurring scenarios where a small change in how we handle the conversation could make a big difference.
From missing empathy in sensitive situations to skipping important Zingtree flows or sending standard vouchers when a proper gift voucher should be created, these controllable moments add up.
Here’s a quick look at some key scenarios, what went wrong, and what the ideal response should look like. Let’s stay sharp and consistent to give our customers the best possible gifting experience! 💚

title: Chat Disconnection and Final Message Automation
details:
Process Update

Moving forward, please ensure strict adherence to the 3-5-0 Rule for Chat Disconnections:

🕒 The maximum hold/dead air time is up to 3 minutes.


⏳ If the customer doesn’t reply after “Is there anything else?” or .fa, wait for 5 minutes of idle time before ending the chat.


✅ If the agent asks, “Is there anything else?” or .fa, and the customer replies “No” or “Thank you”, end the chat immediately after confirmation. (0 minute)

title: Surveys- What you need to know
details:
LOB: CS, MO ● Region: Global ●  Channel: All

We send surveys to customers (CSAT) and merchants (MSAT) in the same format: Smileys rating is horizontal from left-to-right, from bad to good rating: 

All smiley fields are “empty” by default (before customer inputs), to indicate that the customer has not yet selected any response. Once the customer clicks any of the smileys, the selected smiley is highlighted.

Agent experience is ranked as the first question: 
How satisfied are you with our customer/merchant support agent?

Brand experience is ranked as the second question: 
How satisfied are you with Groupon overall?

Text box: ​​How can we improve your experience? is displayed last, under the survey questions to be able to record qualitative data. The text box is shown once the customer/merchant interacts with both of the rating-smileys only.
Ratings are recorded in case survey object as reportable numeric values, which represent the percentage scale ranging from 0% to 100%
=0 =0,25 =0,50 =0,75 =1 

If a customer/merchant changes the response, the new response will be recorded as an additional response in the survey object in Salesforce.

With the expanded survey strategy, multiple feedback instances are now be recorded at the case level, with each response attributed to its originating channel—be it an ended chat, inactive chat, or email interaction.

This allows for more comprehensive tracking and enables deeper, data-driven insights into customer sentiment and service performance across all digital support channels.
 Chat
Surveys are sent for both, ended and inactive chats.
To reduce potential dissatisfaction and confusion:
The survey page will retain the visual illusion of an active chat in the background.
A "Back to Chat" button will allow customers to re-engage before completing the survey.

Email
[CSAT] Surveys are embedded directly in the footer of every support email. This ensures feedback is collected in context, improving both accuracy and response rates.

The embedded survey will redirect customers/merchants to the full survey page for additional comments or insights.

[MSAT] Surveys are sent as a separate email triggered after 24 hours.
Please take a look at the below FAQs

How can I know if the survey was sent to the customer/merchant?
The checkbox “Is CSAT Survey Sent?” (for CS) or “Is MS Survey Sent?” (for MO) IS ticked = survey sent
The checkbox IS NOT ticked = survey not sent
What about ISAT surveys in MO Cases? Are the same questions asked?

No, ISAT survey is sent to internal users only, hence only one question is asked:


If the requester selects “NO” the case gets reopened

What’s this about?
Hi team, 2024 was a fantastic year for Gifting, with strong CSAT growth despite increasing Gift order volumes. As we gear up for Valentine’s Day, we’ve added new banners and redesigned pages on the MBNXT website, Legacy Web & App platforms to create a fresh, festive shopping experience.
Gifting 2024 Recap 

Last year, in summary, we achieved:
An average +85% increase in Gifting orders throughout the year with a +40% increase during our Christmas holiday season alone.
A +28% improvement in Customer Satisfaction (CSAT), despite an increase in Gift order volume. 
Logged +150 bugs/tickets and resolved 204 tickets which drove better customer experience.
Kudos to all of you for your tireless efforts in helping us which resonates with the increase in CSAT. As a matter of fact, Gifting in the past few quarters has had better customer satisfaction than overall Groupon, i.e., customers who reached out regarding gift-related issues received better support than in most of the non-gift-related issues.
Valentine's Day Preparations Across All Platforms
With Valentine’s Day (February 14th) approaching, we’re refreshing our website with festive updates, including revamped homepage branding, app headers, Valentine’s Day banners, and special designs for the Gift Voucher Creator to deliver a vibrant, love-filled experience for our customers!
Continuing efforts to drive Gifting to further heights!
As we carry our winning attitude into 2025, we’re excited to see what this year has in store for Gifting: 
Enhancing the MBNXT app and website: In the first half of 2025, we’re focused on ramping up our MBNXT app and upgrading our website to deliver an even more seamless and delightful Gifting experience.


Revamping customer-facing FAQs: We’re refreshing our Gifting and Gift Card FAQs to provide customers with a more intuitive self-service journey and to answer some of their most common questions right during purchase or redemption.


Expanding Gift Order Share: As was mentioned, gifting doubled over the last year; the plan is not to stop there and aim for repeating the same trend this year as well.

What are my next steps as an Agent?

As we approach one of our most important seasons—Valentine’s Day—it’s essential to stay proactive and fully up to date on the Gifting process. Please take a moment to review the process and always refer to Zingtree for case-handling procedures, especially in these situations:

1️⃣ Customers haven’t received their Gift Vouchers via email or SMS
2️⃣ How to Give as a Gift
3️⃣ How to use a Gift Card

We revamped our Asana Gifting Bug Form to gather accurate and detailed information. This improvement helps us collect the right data to quickly address any bugs that need to be fixed.

Please reach out to your Team Leader or Manager if you have any questions. 
Thank all of you for your support and helping us succeed in Gifting, with the warmest regards,

Linda (c_lvavrikova@groupon.com), Head of Gifting, 
Adithya (a.venkateswaran@groupon.com), Customer Experience Specialist

title: Global Bug Reporting Intake Form 2.0
details:
LOB: All ● Region: All ●  Channel: All

We’re excited to announce that the enhanced version of the Global Bug Reporting (GBR) process is now fully rolled out for both B2B and B2C platforms! This marks a major milestone in our effort to streamline how bugs are reported, tracked, and resolved across Groupon.


What’s New & Why GBR 2.0 is better?
GBR 2.0 delivers a significantly improved experience through a unified and automated process spanning all departments. This results in faster assignment, enhanced visibility into bug status, fewer delays, clearer responsibilities, and improved resolution SLAs. 
Here's what you can expect;
Dedicated B2B, B2C, Bookability and Cloud error & latency Jira forms for bug submission


Transparent ticket tracking through the Jira Service Management portal


Clear communication threads with P&E teams – bi-directional JIRA vs Jira Service management portal. With GBR 2.0, communication between bug reporters and P&E teams is now seamless and fully integrated. Here’s how:


Bi-directional sync: Comments, status updates, and field changes made in Jira (used by engineering teams) automatically reflect in the Jira Service Management portal (used by reporters) — and vice versa. No more fragmented conversations or duplicated updates.


Single source of truth: Everyone involved sees the same ticket, same updates, and same status, whether you're in Jira or JSM.


Consistent communication channel: No need to chase down updates via Gchat or email — use the comment section in the ticket itself to communicate directly with engineering.


4. Automatic notifications: Reporters receive email updates on key changes (e.g., status changes, comments added), so you’re always in the loop without needing to manually check in.


5. Automated routing and assignment to IMOC and Product Managers (see details, slides 13-15)– no guesswork needed


6. Reduced overhead for engineers thanks to automation and better initial triage. In GBR 2.0, automation and improved intake processes significantly cut down on the manual work engineers previously had to handle, including:


Manually triaging incoming tickets to identify the right team or owner


Chasing down missing or unclear information from bug reporters (can be done  via Jira comment)


Duplicating ticket entries across multiple systems (e.g., G-Chat and Jira)


7. Managing ad-hoc status update communications manually


8. With GBR 2.0, we’re introducing a set of key metrics to provide greater transparency into our bug management process:


Resolution Time – how quickly issues are being closed based on priority level


Volume of Bugs – how many bugs are reported over time, by platform and team.


Root Cause Analysis – the underlying reasons behind recurring bugs. Understanding why bugs happen (not just what the bug is) allows us to:


Address systemic issues at their source, not just fix symptoms.


Reduce the number of recurring bugs over time.


Prioritize engineering efforts for maximum business impact.


Improve our products and services at a deeper level, leading to better customer and merchant experiences.


SLA Compliance – whether we’re meeting our agreed resolution timelines.


This improved approach enables all Grouponers to submit a bug using a single form, automatically routes reported bugs to the correct engineering teams based on the details provided in the bug, and applies consistent prioritisation based on business and financial impact. It also allows for the reporter to track bugs through their full lifecycle, with status updates and SLA visibility.

What You Need to Do:
If you're reporting bugs, please make sure you're using the GBR form - providing clear descriptions, impact level, and team ownership where possible. Once submitted, you can monitor your submitted tickets in the Jira Service Management portal. Here's a quick reminder on the step-by-step process;
Access the GBR form
Fill out the required fields (impacted team, priority, description, etc.)
Submit the issue – it will be routed automatically
You’ll receive an email with your ticket and can track updates directly in the Jira Service Management project
Thanks for helping us scale and improve the bug handling across Groupon! Below you will find some quick links to assist you if you experience any issues while bug reporting. Alternatively, please don't hesitate to reach out with any feedback on the process or areas for improvement! 
 Process for Reporters: link

Training Slide Deck – Learn more about the process and benefits
DM or tag @Dawid Ciupiński @Preethi Manjunath for support

title: Issue locating voucher details OR downloading the voucher
details:
LOB: All ● Region: Global ●  Channel: All
Update :  
We’ve merged and updated the “Issue Locating the Voucher” and “Downloading the Voucher” Zingtree paths to streamline resolution and improve customer experience.
Action Required : 
When a customer reports not being able to locate or download a voucher:
Verify Access:


Use the customer’s contact email to search for the voucher.


If found, do not send the PDF immediately.


Educate First:


Ask the customer why they are unable to view the voucher.


Provide guidance on how to access it from their account.


Send PDF Only If Needed:


If the customer is still unable to locate the voucher after education, send the PDF.


Before closing the case:


Add #voucher-sent in the Case Description.


Add the customer’s exact reason for not finding the voucher in the Internal Note.


If the Voucher is Inaccessible:


Escalate to the MO team.


In Case of Multiple Accounts:


Ask the customer to log out and log in to the correct account.


If they still can’t locate the voucher, send the PDF and follow the same internal documentation steps.


Account Deletion Requests:


If the customer can’t log in to delete their account, advise them to email:
 privacy@groupon.[locale]


Update the macro/snippet to include the correct country code.
🚨 Reminder:
The Zingtree path has been fully updated. Please ensure you’re using the revised flow for all relevant scenarios.
